REPORT
The Action Taken Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Ministry of Heavy
Industries and Public Enterprises (Department of Public Enterprises) on the recommendations contained
in the Committee’s Two Hundred and Eighty-Seventh Report on the Demands for Grants (2018-19)
pertaining to Department of Public Enterprises.
2. Action Taken Notes have been received from the Ministry of Heavy Industries and Public Enterprises
(Department of Public Enterprises) in respect of the recommendations contained in the 287 th Report.
These have been categorized as follows:
Chapter I : The recommendations/Observations, which have been accepted by the Ministry.
The Committee notes that the Ministry has accepted its recommendations as mentioned
in the Chapter - I of the Report.
Chapter II : The recommendations/Observations which the Committee does not desire to pursue further
in view of the Government’s replies.
In respect of these recommendations, the Committee is convinced with the logic and
explanation advanced by the Ministry and therefore does not want to pursue them further
for the present.
Chapter III : The recommendations/Observations in respect of which the Committee has not accepted
replies of the Ministry and desires the Ministry to review their replies.
The Committee is not convinced with the replies of the Ministry in respect of
recommendations contained in Chapter - III and desires that the Ministry in the light of
further recommendations/observations of the Committee furnish comments/explanations
thereof.
Chapter IV : The recommendations/Observations in respect of which the Committee desires further
comments of the Ministry.
In respect of recommendations placed in Chapter-IV , the Ministry has either furnished
the interim replies, therefore, the Committee desires that the Ministry may furnish Action
Taken Notes in respect of recommendations categoried in Chapter-IV in detail and to the
point, as per the intention and spirit of the recommendations of the Committee.
3. The details of the Action Taken Replies of the Ministry and further recommendations/observations
of the Committee thereon wherever found necessary are given in the succeeding pages.

CHAPTER -I
THE RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS, WHICH HA VE BEEN ACCEPTED
BY THE MINISTRY
Recommendation/Observation
The Committee notes that compared to the year 20 I 6-17, wherein OPE got a scheme allocation
(BE) of ` 10 crore, for the next two years, i.e, in 2017-18 and 2018-19, the Department got lesser funds
for its schemes. But at the RE stage during 2016-17, funds were reduced to ` 7.24 crore owing to lack of
desired pace of expenditure, adoption of alternative system of MOU and lesser number of Voluntary
Retirement Scheme (VRS) optees in the NER under the CRR Scheme. Further, the Committee finds that
during 2016-17 the Department could only utilize ` 6.72 crore out of the already depleted RE allocation.
Coming to 2017- 18, the Committee finds that the funds for schemes of DPE was only to the tune of
` 8 crore which was slightly reduced to ` 7.67 crore at RE. The Actual Expenditure for the year as on
15.01.2018 is ` 7.29 crore which is almost all of the RE allocated for 2017-18. However, in this regard,
the committee observes that the Department has not furnished the reasons for the reduction of funds at
RE stage for 2017-18. But the Committee presumes that the lack of V oluntary Retirement Scheme (VRS)
optees in the NER under the CRR Scheme continues to be one of the reasons. Taking into account the
above the Committee appreciates the almost cent percent funds utilization achieved by DPE during
2017-18 and recommends that the Department should take measures to maintain such performance during
2018-19 also with regard to their schemes. (Para 15)
Action Taken
The Observations of the Committee have been taken note of and DPE will make all efforts for
maximum utilization of allocated funds.
Recommendation/Observation
The Committee has examined the BE, RE and AE figures of the RDC scheme during the last two
years and the current year. It finds that other than in 2017-18, the two previous years. i.e., 2015-16 and
2016- I 7 saw slashing of Budget Expenditure for the scheme at Revised Estimate stage. The utilization
figure for 2015-16 and 2016-17 were almost 73% and about 93.5%, respectively. The Committee observes
that the reduction of funds at Revised Estimate (RE) stage during the previous two years has not happened
during 2017-18 and the fund utilization is about 88.60%till the second week of January, 2018. Considering
these facts, the Committee is of the opinion that the Department has been able to utilize its fund somewhat
consistently and in an equitable fashion. Accordingly, the Committee recommends that DPE should continue
to strive to shore up its activities under the RDC scheme during 2018-19 as well put in place a better
implementation plan and pace of fund utilization for future. (Para 30)
Action Taken
The observation of the Committee has been noted for compliance during 2018-19) & future for
planned and shored up utilization of funds under RDC Scheme.
Recommendation/Observation
Further, the Committee is aware of the fact that the programmes conducted under the ambit of the
ROC Scheme by OPE can go a long way in positively impacting the performance of CPSEs. The orientation
2

3
session conducted for members appointed as non-official Directors as well as Government Directors of
CPSEs is one example in this regard. The Committee is sure that such moves would aid in the
professionalization of the Boards of the CPSEs concerned as well. (Para 31)
Action Taken
The observation of the Committee would continue to be followed in future by DPE.
Recommendation/Observation
As the Committee analyzed the CAPEX target and the corresponding achievement by various CPSEs,
it is found that the major leveraging of CAPEX has been done by the OIL Sector PSUs, the National
Highway Authority of India (NHAI) and Power Generation and Distribution Companies. Oil and Natural
Gas Corporation CONGC) topped the performance by achieving a target of 218.88%. The Committee
observes that such investment of capital in building the infrastructure of country will have multiplier
effect on the growth of the economy. It also observes that DPE is effectively playing their role by encouraging
CPSEs to pledge more CAPEX by making the same a MoU evaluation parameter . In this regard, the
Committee is of the opinion that the relevance of CPSEs, in the market driven economy with overwhelming
private party presence, is highlighted by the fact that when the private sector were skeptical of such
investment, it was the CPSEs whom met the need of the hour of nation building by pooling in CAPEX for
infrastructure development during the recent past. (Para 34)
Action Taken
The Observation of the Committee have been noted.
Recommendation/Observation
The Committee recommends that DPE may use its good offices to sensitize CPSEs to invest their
CSR funds on activities that are gainful to the society. (Para 43)
Action Taken
The recommendation made by DRPSC has been noted. OPE has been constantly sensitizing CPSE
executives in the workshops/conclaves organized by OPE to invest their CSR funds on the assets/ activities
that arc gainful to the society as per Schedule VIJ of the Companies Act, 2013.

CHAPTER-II
THE RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH THE COMMITTEE DOES NOT DESIRE
TO PURSUE FURTHER IN VIEW OF THE GOVEMMENT’S REPLIES
Recommendation/Observation
Meanwhile, the’ Committee wants to point out that DPE has failed to furnish the reasons quoted by
the Ministry of Finance for not allocating the complete funds ( ` 10.35 crore) sought by the Department
for their schemes during 2018-19. The BE allocated to the Department for the purpose is a lesser amount
of ` 8.50 crore. The said reasons must be furnished to the Committee and it should be specified if it is
anything other than the routine apportioning of the available funds by the Ministry of Finance in the best
possible way. (Para 16)
Action Taken
The BE allocation comes under the jurisdiction of Ministry of Finance. DPE has no reason to offer
on this issue other than that it could be on account of routine apportioning of the available funds by
Ministry of Finance as per their own assessment.
Recommendation/Observation
The Committee find that as the nodal Department of all CPSE, the guidelines issued by DPE
governs important aspects of CPSEs like disposal of movable and immovable assets of CPSEs identified
for closure, revival/restructuring of CPSEs, etc. in this regard, the Committee observes that CPSEs that
are approved for closure, even before the issue of the OPE guidelines on disposal of assets, have also
decided to follow the proposed revised guidelines. Here, the Committee also acknowledges the fact that
the said guidelines of the Department are currently under the consideration of Cabinet Secretariat for
approval of the revision suggested by Committee on Secretaries. The Committee desire that once the
revised guidelines on time bound closure of the sick/loss making CPSEs and disposal of movable and
immovable assets are finalized, the Committee may be apprised of the same. (Para 39)
Action Taken
The Committee will be apprised once, the revised guidelines on time bound closure of sick/loss
making CPSEs and disposal of movable and immovable assets are finalised and approved by the competent
authority.
The revised guidelines on time bound closure of sick/loss making CPSEs and disposal of movable
and immovable assets duly approved by the Cabinet has been submitted to the Committee on 22nd
June, 2018.
4

CHAPTER-III
THE RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH THE COMMITTEE HAS
NOT ACCEPTED THE REPLIES OF THE MINISTRY AND DESIRES THE MINISTRY TO
REVIEW THEIR REPLIES
Recommendation/Observation
The Committee is aware that the realm of CPSEs has recently under gone major changes, especially,
since the Government has decided to restrict itself only to a few selected priority areas of business. Even
the CPSEs that are profitable, but not belonging to specified areas of business, are being disinvested. In
this scenario, the Committee is of the considered opinion that the CPSEs that would remain in operation,
after hiving off of the earlier said non-priority companies, would need clear guidance regarding efficient
functioning and other inputs required to sustain themselves successfully. Here, the Committee takes note
that the mandate of DPE includes the following:
‘Measures aimed at improving performance of Central Public Sector Enterprises and other capacity
building initiatives of Public Sector Enterprises.
Rendering advice relating to revival, restructuring or closure of Public Sector Enterprises including
the mechanisms therefor.”
In the opinion of the Committee, the above mentioned mandates of DPE under the Allocation of
Business Rules, entails DPE to be empowered to play a more proactive role than their current profile.
Accordingly, the Committee recommends that DPE should widen the horizon of its activities, under the
said ambit, to support and facilitate the revival! efficient functioning of CPSEs in future. To achieve
this, the Committee feels that DPE has to think beyond their current set of activities, for which they can
be well endowed with as per the business allocated to them, to actually play the role expected of a nodal
department. (Para 9)
Action Taken
As far as Department of Public Enterprises is concerned, it has issued guidelines on 29.10.2015 for
streamlining the mechanism for revival and restructuring of sick/incipient sick and weak CPSEs. These
guidelines contain provisions for taking pro-active measures for ensuring efficient functioning of the
CPSEs. These guidelines are implemented by the administrative Ministries/Departments.
In respect of proposals for revival/restructuring formulated by the administrative Ministries/
Departments, DPE gives its comments/views/suggestions, if the proposals are referred to it during inter-
ministerial consultation process.
Further Recommendations/Observations
The Committee is constrained to point out that the reply of the Government has completely
missed the essence of the recommendation of the Committee which was for the Department of
Public Enterprises (DPE) to playa m o rc proactive role than what they currently essay. It was also
brought out in the recommendation why this WaS needed and how it could be done.
The Committee’s opinion was that in the background of the Government’s policy to continue
with only priority sector CPSEs, DPE should widen its horizon of activities to come up with more
5

6
effective and intuitive measures to guide the CPSEs (that operate in the said priority areas identified
by the Government) for their successful performance. In the absence of such support and guidance
for their efficient functioning, from the DPE, the Committee apprehends that these CPSEs which
have been identified by the Government under selected priority areas of business, would also be
ordained to meet a similar adversarial fate as their brethren CPSEs belonging to non-priority
areas of business. However, the reply of the Government completely missed this point and has
concentrated on the role of DPE on the revival/restructuring of CPSEs. The recommendation was
for DPE to think out of the box and to contribute proactively by utilizing the leverage available
for this under the current Allocation of Business for DPE. The Committee hence reiterates its
recommendation and wants a cogent reply in this regard.
Recommendation/Observation
With regard to disposal of land and other assets of CPSEs, the Committee recommends that DPE
being the nodal Department of all CPSEs should collect from the respective administrative Ministries/
Departments the relevant data and compile and maintain the same with them. (Para 40)
Action Taken
As per guidelines issued by DPE on 7.9.2016, CPSEs under closure in consultation with
administrative Ministry shall dispose of their assets (movable and immovable). The details of such disposal
will be available with the administrative Ministry.
Further Recommendations/Observations
The Committee while noting the Government’s reply impress upon the DPE to collect the
details of the land and other assets of CPSEs as and when the same are disposed of by the respective
Administrative Ministry/Department and inform the Committee of such details.
Recommendation/Observation
Further , the Committee takes note of the information submitted by DPE as collected by them
from DIP AM about the strategic disinvestment of CPSEs and the proceeds that accrue to the Government
exchequer from sale/disinvestment of CPSES. It is found that receipts from disinvestment during 2017- 18
is expected to be around 
` 1,00,000 crore while an amount of ` 80,000 crore is supposed to accrue to
Government during 2018-19. The Committee is aware that the Government has decided to engage in
business only in a few selected areas of ‘High Priority’. However, the Committee is of the firm opinion
that while making a decision to disinvest CPSEs especially those are profit making, the Government
should give due consideration to the jobs that are supported by those CPSEs, the track record of their
contribution to the national economy, their CAPEX creation potential and also their role in balancing
the social/regional fabric. Regarding the revival/restructuring/modernization of CPSEs, the Committee
observes that timely approval of these plans, with accurate cost estimates, availability of funds with
the Government and the timely disposal of such finds are crucial factors. Accordingly, the Committee
recommends that a defined portion of the proceeds from disinvestment should be kept aside by the
Government for funding the revival/restructuring/modernization proposals of CPSEs as identified
approved by the Government. In this manner, the Government can extend a hand holding to the select
sick CPSES that have the potential to turn around and sustain itself in future.
(Para 41)

7
Action Taken
As the subject matter concerns to Department of Investment and Public Asset Management and
Department of Economic Affairs, DPE had requested them to provide information. DIAPM has replied as
under:
DIPAM has noted the recommendation of the Committee and stated that at present the receipts
from the disinvestment are credited to the National Investment Fund (NIF) and used for the following
approved purposes:
(i) Subscribing to the shares being issued by the CPSEs including PSBs and Public Sector Insurance
Companies on rights basis so as to ensure that 51% ownership of the Government in those
CPSEs /PSBs /Insurance Companies, is not diluted.
(ii) Preferential allotment of shares of the CPSE to promoters as per SEBI (Issue of Capital and
Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2009 so that Government shareholding does not go
down below 51 % in all cases where the CPSE is going to raise fresh equity to meet its Capex
programme.
(iii) Recapitalization of public sector banks and public sector insurance companies.
(iv) Investment by Government in RRBs/IIFCL/NABARD/Exim Bank;
(v) Equity infusion in various Metro projects;
(vi) Investment in Bhartiya Nabhikiya Vidyut Nigam Limited and Uranium Corporation of India
Ltd., and
(vii) Investment in Indian Railways towards capital expenditure.
Further Recommendations/Observations
The Committee finds that the reply of the Government (Department of Investment and
Public Asset Management) narrates only the manner in which the receipts from disinvestment
are currently used through the National Investment Fund (NIF). The Committee is of the view
that it does not reflect any ostensible use of these receipts. The existing system, the Committee
feels is unfair towards CPSEs that have contributed to nation building at the times of requirement.
Accordingly, the Committee reiterates its recommendation that a defined portion of the proceeds
from disinvestment of CPSEs should be kept aside for funding of the revival/restructuring/
modernization proposals of CPSEs.

CHAPTER-IV
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH THE COMMITTEE DESIRE
FURTHER COMMENTS OF THE MINISTRY
Recommendation/Observation
The Committee finds that there is a mismatch between the reflection of fund utilization of Schemes
in NER as reflected in the Demands (No. 45) Document relating to the Department and the figures for the
same as submitted by the Department to the Committee. In this regard, the Committee takes into account
the explanation given by the Department that from 2014-15 onwards allocation of funds in the NER was
only made under grant-in-aid. However, the Committee also finds it very unrealistic that a ‘Nil’  fund
utilization against NER in the Demands Document for the years 2015-2016 and 2016-17 has been shown
as ‘fully utilized’  by the Department in reply to a query by the Committee. The Committee wonders as to
how such gross misinterpretation of figures could take place and finds itself in a quandary as to which of
the figures ref1ecting the actual spending is to be taken as correct and genuine. The Committee accordingly,
recommends that the Department should rectify such misrepresentation of Budget figures in their Demands
Document. (Para 20)
Action Taken
The utilization of funds against allocated amount in NER during 2015-16 and 2016-17 is not reflected
in Demand of Grants document (No. 45) relating to Department of Public Enterprises (OPE). This is
because of the fact that allocation as shown against NER in DDG is ‘Parking Head’. Against this allocation,
re-appropriation from ‘Parking Head’ to ‘Functional Head’ is required to be done for incurring expenditure,
as per laid down procedure. Accordingly, funds for the amount of ` 0.51 crore and ` 0.72 crore after re-
appropriation under Functional Head has been utilized in NER in 2015-16 and 2016-17 and this has not
been ref1ected in DDG (Demand No. 45), being the Parking Head. The observation of the Committee has
also been taken note of by the Department.
Recommendation/Observation
The Committee finds, as witnessed during the preceding years, the funds allocated to CRR at
the BE stage were reduced during RE for the year 2017-18 also. But the utilization of the RE amount
looks better during 2017-18 compared to 2016-17. The Department has been constantly taking the
plea that the lack of VRS optees under the scheme in the NER is the reason for incomplete utilization
of funds and the consequent surrender of funds to Non-Lapsable Central Pool of Resources of NER
for the year 2016-17.further, the Committee observes that although the targeted number of persons
are more or less getting trained under the scheme, and as such there is near total achievement in the
training sector, however , their redeployment hovers around 51 to 52%, only. In this regard, the Committee
is of the opinion that by utilizing the domain expertise of NSDC, The Department should further
enhance the redeployment of persons trained under the scheme for gainful employment. For this,
focused identification of the market demand for specific skills is required and training should be
conducted to cater to such requirement. In the Committee’ s opinion, considering the fact that the
VRS optees trained under the scheme are already skilled in a given profession, channelizing their
acquired skills to help find new avenues of employment wouldn’t be that difficult. Taking the above
facts into account, the Committee recommends that DPE should take steps to improve redeployment
8

9
of VRS optees trained under CRR scheme and the feedback that could be available through the
ongoing third party evaluation of the scheme, should be made use of for the purpose.
(Para 25)
Action Taken
As per Project Completion Report submitted by NSDC for the year 2016-17 redeployment during
the year stood at 56%. This includes both VRS/VSS optees as well as dependents. With inclusion of
dependents redeployment rate has improved.
Undertaking CRR training in association with NSDC following National Skill Qualification Framework
(NSQF) as per National Occupational Standard (NOS) is likely to have higher redeployment rate. The
observations of the Committee were also brought to the notice of NSDC in the meeting held with Ministry
of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship and NSDC at DPE on 21.05.2018

Recommendation/ Observation

Recommendation/Observation
The Committee understands that the gradual transition to pure EVs is an inevitability considering
the limited fossil fuel reserves and heightened environmental concerns. However, it has felt that the
path of transformation needs a lot of coordinated and well thought out planning from the part of the
Government, with the partnership of the Auto Industry. A synchronized platform involving the relevant
Ministries and other stakeholders need to be set up for policy formulation and implementation. Further ,
the Committee perceives that EV penetration in the Country would critically depend on the development
of indigenous battery technology and the creation/setting up of charging infrastructure dovetailed by
appropriate charging technology. Also, the Committee is of the considered opinion that the economic
ramification of transformation to pure EV technology has to be given priority by the Government,
taking into account the fact that any laxity in proper planning and implementation could affect millions
of jobs in the auto sector . Such an impact on jobs would be unaffordable to the economy of a developing
country like India. The Department should make concerted efforts in planning a roadmap to re-deploy
the employees in the conventional Auto Sector, who would be displaced with the change over to electric
mobility.
Taking all of the above into account, the Committee recommends that the Government should come up
with a well spelt out road map based on empirical studies before pushing hard for change over to pure BY
technology. In the opinion or the Committee, gradual shift, taking the route of promoting appropriate hybrid
technology, could be one of the adoptable methods in this direction. The F AME- India scheme under DHI is
an ideal vehicle which could be widened in scope and magnitude to accommodate the challenging needs of
the Country’s gradual shift to the Electric Mobility. The Committee is well aware that the stakes are high for
the Country in terms of the environmental benefit the changeover can offer and also in terms of the weaning
away from import dependence on fossil fuels. (Para 36 & 37)
Action Taken
National Council for Electric Mobility (NCEM) and National Board of Electric Mobility (NBEM),
which are chaired by Hon’ble Minister for Heavy Industries & Public Enterprises and by Secretary (Heavy
Industry) respectively, and are having members from various stakeholders including Government Departments/
Ministries, Industry Associations and various Original Equipments Manufacturers (OEMs), are already in
place to propagate electric mobility and manufacture of electric vehicles (including hybrid vehicles) and
their components.
In addition, the Department has already included the Industry Representatives from Society of Indian
Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM), Automotive Component Manufacturers Association (ACMA) and Society
of Manufacturing of Electric Vehicles (SMEV) in the Committees of the Department concerning Auto Sector.
Further, there are representatives from various stakeholder Ministries and Automotive Industries in the
Development Council of Automobile & Allied Industries (DCAAI) of the Department. Hence, it is evident
that the Department of Heavy Industry is taking care of Private Sector involvement in the Policy Formulations/
Implementation etc.

4
As far as synchronised platform involving the relevant Ministries and other stakeholders for policy
formulation and implementation is concerned, in addition to the DCAAI mentioned above, NITI Aayog
has recently been designated as the nodal agency for promotion of Electric Vehicles/clean mobility solution.
Accordingly, the NITI Aayog, in consultation with all stakeholders, is already in the process of formulating
a strategy to scale up transformative mobility for uptake of Zero Emission Vehicles and ancillary
technologies.
Regarding development of indigenous battery technology and the creation/setting up of charging
infrastructure, the Ministry of Electronics & Information Technology (MEJTY), under their M-SIPS program,
is already extending capital subsidy for setting up of units for electronic/ telecommunication components
which may be utilised for battery technology. Through the scheme component or Pilot Project, some charging
infrastructure projects have already been approved by DHI.
It may be mentioned here that at present there is no proposal under consideration of Department of
Heavy Industry for targeted complete transformation or vehicles technology from ICE based technology to
Electric Powertrain based technology for vehicles. DHI notes the views of the Committee in the matter and
agrees that changeover to electric mobility must not disrupt the existing Auto Industry. In fact, DHI proposes
an incremental switchover of technology gradually and the Committee may, therefore, have no apprehension
of job loss in auto sector.
However, the valuable suggestions of the Hon’ble Committee for gradual shift from ICE to Electric
Mobility under FAME-India Scheme have been noted for compliance.

THE RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH THE COMMITTEE HAS

Recommendation/Observation
Regarding the operating CPSEs, under the administrative control of Department of Heavy Industry,
the Committee notices that their number has begun to dwindle since 2016-17. From a total of 31 in 2016-17,
they have come down to 24 in 2017-18 and curr ently, the number of operating CPSEs under DBI has been
reduced to 22. According to the data submitted by OPE before the Committee, amongst the Ministries/
Departments of Government of India it is DHI that has seen the largest attrition rate of CPSEs - 10 that
have been approved for closure and 6 that have been approved for strategic disinvestment.
In this regard, the Committee takes into cognisance the fact that depending on the NITI Aayog’ s
classification of ‘High Priority’ areas for Government Ownership, CPSEs which are in profit or those that
can very well be revived/restructured can also be strategically disinvested/closed, if they do not fall under
the priority areas. Accordingly, the Committee recommends that DHI should start classifying CPSEs under
it, in tune with the ‘High Priority’ areas identified for Government ownership. Such classification would
help the Department focus its attention and funds on CPSEs that would be identified for retention under
Government ownership as per extant policy. In the opinion of the Committee, this would in turn give more
meaning to the Department’s Mission and Vision statements. (Para 6&7)
Action Taken
DHI undertakes appraisals of each loss-making CPSEs wherein appropriate response to the performance
of individual CPSEs is determined in consultation with stakeholders after periodic appraisal. NITI Aayog has
scanned almost all the companies under DHI and based on the criteria/parameters of high priority/low
priority areas have recommended some CPSEs for disinvestment or closure. CPSEs found chronically sick
are disinvested or closed down after payment of attractive V oluntary Retirement Scheme (VRS)/V oluntary
Separation Scheme (VSS) compensation to employees. As per this practice, the Government has already
decided to close some of the CPSEs under this Department namely, Tungabhadra Steel Products Ltd.,
Hindustan Cables Ltd., HMT Watches Ltd .. I-IMT Chinar Watches Ltd., HMT Bearings Ltd., Kota Unit of
Instrumentation Ltd. and Tractor Division of HMT Ltd. These CPSEs suffered sickness due to a number of
factors including poor order booking, shortage of working capital. surplus manpower. obsolete plant and
machinery, stiff competition from private sector, cheaper imports and difficulty to adjust to changing market
conditions. In addition, the Government has also decided for 100% disinvestment of Bridge & Roof Co.
Ltd., Scooters India Ltd. and Bharat Pumps & Compressors Ltd., Disinvestment of 100% shareholding of
the concerned CPSE in Hindustan Ncwsprints Ltd. (a subsidiary of Hindustan Paper Co Ltd.) to strategic
buyer through two stage auction process, Units of Cement Corporation of India Ltd. to be disinvested
where it is legally permissible to strategic buyer through two stage auction process and Merger of Engineering
Projects (India) Ltd. with similar by placed CPSEs. Subsequently, on the suggestion of NITI Aayog and
upon approval of Cabinet /CCEA, DHI is pursuing the laid down course of action. As such the attrition rate
is higher.
Further Recommendations/Observations
The Committee observes that the reply of the Government does not address the crux of its

recommendation. DHI has furnished the details of the CPSEs recommended/identified by the NITI
Aayog for disinvestment/closure as well as the reasons behind their poor performance and the

recommended that the CPSEs under the fold of DHI, which fall under the ‘High Priority’ category
as identified by the Government, shall be concentrated upon by DHI for their better performance so
as to enable their continued retention under Government ownership as per extant policy. Besides,
in the absence of such categorisation of CPSEs as those falling under ‘High Priority’ business area
and those falling under ‘Low Priority’ business area, an apprehension is felt that the Department

utilisation of funds would be meaningless as ultimately the CPSEs of ‘Low Priority’ business areas
would meet a fate of closure/disinvestment, without getting a chance of revival. The Committee is
of the opinion that this would help the Department to concentrate precious resources on ‘High

have conceded as a fact. Further, such a move would also lend more meaning to DHI’s Mission and

Recommendation/Observation
Also, the Committee is of the opinion that it would be prudent for DHI to study the goods/services
offered by the CPSEs intended/identified for closure or strategic disinvestment and understand the manner
in which the void likely to be created in the market due to the absence of Government ownership of these
CPSEs is going to get filled. If such demands are proposed to be met by imports, including cheap second-
hand machinery/goods, rather than by domestic production, then it must be assumed that the closure/strategic
disinvestment would be antithetical to national priority of promoting domestic production and ‘Make in
India’ initiative and would be a matter of great worry. Accordingly, the Committee recommends that the
Department should commission a research study to find reasons as to why they are losing CPSEs dealing
with goods/services under the Heavy Industries Sector. The study should also focus on the market demand
currently being met by these CPSEs and how the said demand would be met in case of their closure/strategic
disinvestment. (Para 8)
Action Taken
Those Companies which have been recommended for closure/disinvestment were sick/loss making/
unviable for past many years because a lot of private players began manufacturing these products at more
efficient and competitive prices. The gaps in manufacturing of products (like watches, tractors, cables, etc.)
/demand created by the closure of these companies are already filled up by the private manufacturers. Hence
it is unlikely that the import of these products will increase.
Further Recommendations/Observations
The Committee finds that the reply of the Government is in contradiction to their own answer
to the recommendation of the Committee as contained in paragraphs 6 and 7 wherein the Government
has cited import of cheap products as one of the reasons contributing to CPSEs turning to loss
incurring. But in the instant reply, the Government claims that it is unlikely for such imports to
increase.
Here, the Committee would like to clarify the reason for suggesting a research study, is to
find out the alternative sources for the products in the market which have hitherto been catered to

reply concentrates only on CPSEs that have been identified for closure till now. However, the
Committee would like to stress that the study proposed above should cover all CPSEs under DHI. In
the opinion of the Committee, if the products of such CPSEs are expected to be replaced in the
market by imported goods, especially to the detriment of domestic producers, then the Government
would have enough reasons to revisit their decision of disinvestment. The Committee feels that
import of goods from China is adversely affecting the economy of the country as well as the industrial

this lacuna ‘which otherwise can hinder the growth of India’s Capital Goods Sector. (Para 57)
Action Taken
Under the Scheme for Enhancement of Competitiveness in Indian Capital Goods Sector, a Test and
Certification Centre of Earth Moving Machinery has been proposed to be set lip through a Special Purpose
Vehicle (SPV) with a cost or `100.00 crore to be funded by the Department of Heavy Industry. Such Test
and Certification Centre is under active consideration or the Department and the Automotive Research
Association of India (ARAI) has been requested to work in collaboration with Indian Construction Equipment
Manufacturers Association (ICEMA) in preparing the proposal for setting up of the Construction, Earthmoving,
Material Handling and Mining Machinery (CEMM) Equipment Test Centre. Detailed Project Implementation
Report (DPIR) is being prepared by ARAI.
With regard to the funding of Test and Certification Centre, it is mentioned that under the present

12
Capital Goods Scheme, the projects worth ` 572.22 crore have already been approved and thereby the said
Centre can be set up after the availability of additional funds under the present scheme or after the approval
of the new scheme.
Further Recommendations/Observations
The Committee finds that the reply of the Government does not address the issue flagged by
the Committee in its recommendation regarding the delay in setting up of Test and Certification
Centre under the Scheme for Enhancement of Competitiveness in Indian Capital Goods Sector.
The reply mentions that such Test and Certification Centres is under active consideration and the
Detailed Project Implementation Report (DPIR) is being prepared by Automotive Research Association
of India (ARAI). Details regarding the funding of the Test and Certification Centre have also not
been specified in the reply. Keeping this in view the Committee reiterates its recommendation to
expedite the implementation of the Test and Certification Centre and to secure the requisite fund
for the same without any further delay and furnish the status to the Committee.
Recommendation/Observation
The Committee notes that for the first year, within the fold of DHI, CMTI had been earmarked with
` 10 crore as BE for part payment of salary of the employees of the institute. The Committee also takes note
of the submission of DBI that the Institute has the potential to spearhead R&D efforts in the field of
Machine Tools and also help bridge the technology gap affecting the players of Capital Goods Sector in
India. It is felt that such an institute should be accorded special status under the ‘Make in India” programme.
The Committee recommends that DHI should pursue this matter on priority and endeavour to setup more
such institutes at different Capital Goods Sector hub of the country as it was observed that only a meagre 0.5
per cent of entire turnover is being increased in R&D. vis-a vis all average of 2 per cent investment ill
developing countries and 5-6 % investment in the developed nations. Further, the Committee also recommends
that the institute should be allocated budgetary support to strengthen its core R&D activities that could
enhance manufacturing competitiveness in the country. (Para 73)
Action Taken
CMTI, a unique; premier Applied R&D institute is offering technology solutions to the manufacturing
Sector for more than five decades. In line with its mandate, the Institute has always tried hard to bring in
new technologies, assimilate and disseminate them for the benefit of the Indian manufacturing sector.
Leveraging its strength in manufacturing technology, CMTI has also developed competencies and capabilities
in Complex and Special purpose machine building involving design, manufacturing, assembly & testing and
is a one-stop shop for ideation to realization. Realizing fully functional first time manifestations, specifically
denied technologies, is the primary strength of CMTI.
Further Recommendations/Observations
The Committee had recommended the Central Manufacturing Technology Institute (CMTI)
shall be accorded special status under the ‘Make in India’ programme which should be pursued by
DHI on priority. It was also recommended that the institute should be allocated Budgetary Support
to strengthen its core R&D activities. In their reply, DHI has stated that CMTI has submitted
Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) for the consideration of DHI which will be considered based on
availability of funds and that several projects of CMTI are funded under the Scheme are for

13
Enhancement of Competitiveness in Indian Capital Goods Sector. However, the Committee finds
that the DHI has maintained silence on its recommendation regarding according of special status
for CMTI under the ‘Make in India’ programme in their reply. Accordingly, the Committee reiterates
its recommendation to pursue on priority the accordance of special status to CMTI and continue
budgetary support to the institute to strengthen its core R&D activities. Further, it is also the
considered opinion of the Committee that allocation of funds to CMTI may be given priority based
on the merit of the proposals and taking into consideration the fact that India lags behind in core
R&D activities and the Government is planning to invest heavily on expansion of R&D in near
future and develop the country into a Global Innovation hub by 2020.
Recommendation/Observation
As part of the oral evidence before the Committee in connection with the examination of Demands
2018-19 or DHI, Secretary, DBI interalia opined that “........... sometimes Government’ s neglect may be
good for the CPSEs. Maybe they will be healthier on their ows.” Further, it is in the knowledge of the
Committee that the Government has decided to engage in business only in a few selected areas of operation
like in the spheres of national security, sovereign functions at arms length like the exploration of natural
resources, etc and market imperfections and Public Purpose. Notwithstanding this, the Committee feels that
the Government should take a judicious view of the track record of the CPSEs concerned before applying
the “high priority” principle devised by them to close down/disinvest CPSEs. Also, in support to CPSEs, the
Committee takes into account the deposition of Department of’ Public Enterprises as part of their Demands
for Grants before the Committee that CPSIs have proved their relevance with their ability to plough in
CAPEX (investment) in recent times, while the private sector held itself back, which had helped the Government
keep its infrastructure investment targets active. Therefore, the Committee is of the opinion that while
precious public money should not be wasted on CPSEs that turn redundant, those public enterprises which
have stood the test of time can and should have some hand holding in the form of budgetary support from
the part of the Government. Besides, by their own Mission statement, the Department has a mandate to
provide necessary support to CPSEs in order to improve their overall performance and in the opinion of the
Committee, DHI should leave no stone unturned to fulfil this responsibility vested on them. (Para 80)
Action Taken
All CPSEs of DHI have been screened by NITI Aayog in terms of extant laid down parameters of
‘high priority’/ ‘low priority’ areas. Based on this some of the CPSEs are being closed down and some are
under disinvestment process.
Further Recommendations/Observations
The Committee takes note of the reply of the Department, but is of the opinion that its
recommendation shall be reiterated since it feels the CPSEs have to be given credit to the contributions
they have made towards nation building. The Committee feels that the Government has to take
into account the track record of a CPSE before applying the ‘High Priority’ and ‘Low Priority’
principle devised by them for disinvestment/closure of CPSEs. Accordingly, it is again recommended
that those CPSEs which have stood the test of time should be handheld by the Government, to the
extent possible, in the form of budgetary support. The Committee feels that DHI will be well
within its rights to suggest a review of the extant policy especially taking into consideration the
relevance of CAPEX cushion the CPSEs have been providing to the Government to sail through

14
some tough economic situations. Even under the present scenario, when the Government is fixing
targets for CAPEX for CPSEs to enhance the growth of the economy, its relevance should be
reviewed positively.

CHAPTER-IV
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH THE COMMITTEE
DESIRE FURTHER COMMENTS OF THE MINISTRY
Recommendation/Observation
Regarding the report of the C&AG on the performance audit of NATRiP, the Committee desires that
it be furnished with the findings thereof as and when the Report is available. (Para 24)
Action Taken
When Final Audit Report is received from CAG, it will be furnished to the Committee.
Recommendation/Observation
Further, while analysing the fund allocation and utilization under NATRiP in 2016-17 and 2017-18,
the Committee noted that in 2016-17 the fund has been completely utilized and for the current financial
year, the utilization is 89% of RE by the end of January, 2018, Likewise, the Committee hopes that for the
year, 2018-19, the Department would take appropriate measures to utilize the fund allocated effectively as
per their submission made before the Committee. Here, the Committee also takes into account the submission
of the Department that during 2017-18 they faced certain legal road blocks mainly due to delinquent
contractors. It was also seen that the slow take off at certain facilities is due to hitches in the bidding
process. However, since most of the facilities have now surpassed the legal problems and troubled bidding
process, the Committee expects that there shall not be any further delays in the future and the scheduled
completion time of July, 2019 would be adhered to. It is for DHI to ensure this, by providing timely interventions
to avoid such roadblocks in future. (Para 25)
Action Taken
Under RE 2017-18, funds to the tune of ` 307.00 crore were allocated to NATRIP for completion of
various project activities.
Up to 31
st March, 2018 expenditure to the tune of ` 345.46 crore has been made by NATRIP which is
112.53% (approx) of RE and same has been met out from Grants as well as refund of Land Cost by
UPSIDC amounting ` 36.52 crore.
NATRIP has been allocated for FY 2018-19 funds to the tune of ` 378.88 crore, of which ` 178.88
crore is against Grant-in-Aid and ` 200.00 crore is loan. It is worth mentioning that progress of various
facilities of NATRIP is being monitored regularly at the highest levels in order to ensure completion of the
project by June, 2019 as per CCEA approved timeline
Recommendation/Observation
For the year 2018-19, the allocation for AUSC is only 
` 100 crorc whereas the CCEA approved fund
for the year is ` 608 crore. Such humongous difference in the planned expenditure and the Actual allocation
compels the Committee to presume that there are enough reasons to be apprehensive about the progress of
the Mission Mode project as pace of the project execution decides the fund allocation. Going as per the
figures approved by the CCEA, till now, the fund allocation of the project should have been 
` 729.00 crore
whereas the actual allocation is ` 90 crore (Revised Estimates, 2017-18) and ` 100 crore (Budget Estimates,
15

16
2018-19) totalling to only ` 190 crore. The Committee also takes note of the fact that the Department is
confident of meeting the timeline of the project as submitted by them.
Taking the above situation into account, the Committee cannot but express its displeasure at this
juncture about the way the Mission Mode AUSC supervised by the Principal Scientific Advisor to the
Government of India is progressing. The Committee accordingly recommends that DHI, as-the primary
contributor to the project, should take appropriate measures to improve the pace of the implementation of
the project in coordination with other stakeholders. (Para 68 & 69)
Action Taken
Apart from ` 90 crore released as observed by the Committee, ` 30 crore have also been released by
DHI in March, 2018 itself. Hence the whole amount i.e. ` 1 20 crore allocated for 2017-18 has been released
by DHI and the same has been utilized by AUSC Project Mission Directorate.
For the year 2018-19, CCEA had approved ` 608 Crore for the AUSC R&D Project. The allocation of
` 100 crore (BE) for the year 2018-19 for the A USC R&D Project is less than the projected requirement.
The fund allocation to various schemes including AUSC project has been made by the Department keeping
in view the total allocation ( ` 1125.73 crore) intimated by Ministry of Finance to the Department.
Fund requirement of at least ` 425 crore for the year 2018-19 has been envisaged by the BHEL- AUSC
Project Mission Directorate for the Financial Year 2018-19, against the anticipated requirement of ` 608
crore, as per CCEA approval.
Additional fund will be sought by Department through Supplementary Demands for Grants to ensure
timely execution of this R&D project.
It may be worth mentioning that the progress so far is as per schedule and the work plan for 2018-19
is also expected to be achieved.
Recommendation/ Observation
The Committee notes that HPC has been in trouble since the year 2009-10 which began with the
shortage of bamboo, its primary raw material. Further, many other external factors added to the woes of the
company over the succeeding years. Alongwith such reasons the necessity for the upgradation of plant and
machinery also weighed down the performance of HPC. A revival/restructuring plan or the company has
been pending approval of the Government since 2016-17. During 2017-18, Rs 95 crore was allocated as BE
in anticipation of approval for the revival, but the Committee finds that this money had to be withdrawn at
RE stage because the revival was yet to be approved by the competent authority. Funds have again been
provisioned for 2018-19 hoping for the approval. Further, the Committee understands that there has been a
new development in the matter which is the move to engage an Operations & Maintenance (O&M) partner
to run HPC. Regarding approval to the revival/restructuring of HPC, the Committee apprehends that further
delay in the matter can seriously jeopardise the viability of revival of HPC. The Committee expects that the
Government will show the requisite urgency in approving the revival/restructuring plan of the company and
hopes that the engagement of O&M partner does not herald the privatisation of HPC. With respect to the
impetus given to National Bamboo Mission, the Committees wants DHI to coordinate with the Ministry of
Agriculture/ National Bamboo Mission/ Ministry of DoNER to ensure ample raw material supply to HPC by
way of methods like captive farming promoted amongst small and marginal local bamboo farmers as per the
provisions of the Mission. (Para 88)

17
Action Taken
A draft CCEA note for revival of HPC through engagement of O&M partner has been circulated for
inter-ministerial consultations. Once the approval of Cabinet is obtained, further action towards floating of
tender and finalisation of O&M partner would be taken. Thereafter necessary action to consult stakeholders
for ensuring ample raw material shall be taken.
Recommendation/ Observation
The Committee’s summarisation of the approach of the Government towards the modernization of
HEC is that the Company is to be strategically disinvested; a private partner is to be brought in to run the
company on JV basis and also to hive off non-core assets like surplus land of HEC to a separate SPV and
be monetized. In this connection, the Committee notes that apart from the idea of monetization of its land,
the other two are new to Committee. Said this, the Committee is yet not aware whether these proposals of
DHI are in conformity with the recommendations of Dr. Saraswat Committee which have been pending with
the Government, for final approval, for more than a year- now. Further, the Committee notes that the
Department holds a view that the present financial condition of the Company and the repealed failures of
the past revival packages have prompted them to mull the new ideas. Here, the Committee is not convinced
of the reasons ascribed by DHI, keeping in view the fact that the alter the revival packages of 2005 to 2008,
HEC had shown profit till 2012-13. Gut it remains a fact that the said revival packages had not focussed on
modernization of plant and machinery of HEC but were mainly debt waivers and financial restructuring.
The Committee believes that the present financial condition of HEC is the result of the lack of foresight in
not supplementing the waivers of debts with modernization plans, which ultimately caused the Company to
slip back to losses again. The Committee opines that as the administrative Department of HEC, DHI cannot
absolve itself the responsibility for the current situation at HEC. Keeping in view the above, the Committee
recommends that DHI should give full weightage to the recommendation of Dr. Saraswat Committee which
had favoured the revival of HEC by approving the revival plan proposed by the Company, before contemplating
measures like strategic disinvestment. Besides, the Committee is highly critical of the delay on the part of
the Government in arriving at a decision regarding the revival of HEC. Administrative delay of this kind
adds to the misery of CPSEs awaiting revival. It is surprising that revival/restructuring of CPSEs remains
long drawn despite the efforts of the Government claim of hastening them up. (Para 99)
Action Taken
The recommendation/observation of the Committee in respect of HEC has been noted by the Department.
The recommendations of Saraswat Committee are still under consideration of the Government and no
finality has been achieved as yet.
Recommendation/Observation
The Committee wants to cite the case of NEP A as an extreme case of administrative apathy and
indifference towards the revival of a CPSE with an unignorable developmental legacy. The Committee finds
that BIFR, for a company referred to them in 1998, approved a Rehabilitation Scheme for revival of NEPA
in 2014, based on cost estimation as a part of its original Techno-Economic Feasibility Report (TEFR),
formulated in 2010. It will be anybody’ s guess that approval of a cost estimation made in 2010, as such in
2014, plagued by further implementation delay, would only result in further conundrum for the Company.
This is exactly where NEP A finds itself today. On the Government’s part, they have released their part of

18
funds as included in the total cost of RMDP of NEPA. However , it was obvious from the submission of DHI
that without the loan portion materializing from the banks, far which the banks were insisting on ‘Government
guarantee, the execution of RMDP would remain incomplete. Now, the revised cost estimate is Rs 434 crore
and the process for securing an approval for this amount from the competent authority is underway. The
progress made towards securing loan with or without Government guarantee, has not been furnished to the
Committee. Further. the Committee is aware of the recommendation of NITI Aayog with respect to NLPA
which is that the revival process of NEP A may be permitted to complete and then the Company may be
reviewed for strategic disinvestment. The Committee is of the view that if’ the current state of affairs is
allowed to prevail, the revival of EPA might remain a mirage. Accordingly, the Committee recommends that
DHI should come up with proactive and fast-tracked measures, with accelerated inter-departmental
coordination, if deemed required, to revive/restructure NEP A, taking every care to avoid any further delay.
It is further recommended that the decision whether or not to provide Government guarantee for obtaining
the bank loan portion of the funds for executing the RMDP should also not be procrastinated any further
because clarity in this regard will give a better assessment of the availability and sources of funds for the
revival of NEP A. (Para 102)
Action Taken
DHI has already prepared a draft Cabinet Note containing proposal for budgetary support for revised
cost estimates of the RMDP, payment of pending salary/wages and statutory dues and for funding VRS for
employees of Nepa Limited after due and in depth deliberations and had circulated the same for inter-
ministerial consultation on 11.12.2017. To reach a consensus on the course of direction to be taken meetings
are being taken with the stakeholders to discuss the comments received on the Cabinet note and finalize the
same for consideration of the Cabinet.
Recommendation/Observation
During the presentation in connection with examination of the DFG-2018-19, the Secretary, DHI has
stated that land assets of HCL at Hyderabad and Asansol are slated to be disposed off as per guidelines
framed by DPE. The Secretary also informed the first round of bidding process had been completed recently,

Committee accordingly desires that DHI may in collaboration with the authorities concerned ensure that

REPORT
The Action Taken Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Ministry of Micro,
Small and Medium Enterprises on the recommendations contained in the Committee’s Two Hundred Eighty
Eighth Report on Demands for Grants (2018-19) pertaining to the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium
Enterprises.
2. Action Taken Notes received from the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises in respect of
the recommendations contained in the 288 th Report have been categorized as follows:-
Chapter I : The Recommendations/Observations, which have been accepted by the Ministry.
The Committee is pleased to observe that the Ministry has accepted its recommendations as
mentioned in the Chapter - I of the Report.
Chapter II : The Recommendations/Observations which the Committee does not desire to pursue further
in view of the Government’s replies.
In respect of these recommendations, the Committee is convinced with the logic and
explanations advanced by the Ministry and therefore does not want to pursue them further
for the present.
Chapter III : The Recommendations/Observations in respect of which the Committee has not accepted
the replies of the Ministry and desires the Ministry to review their reply.
The Committee is not convinced with the replies of the Ministry in respect of recommendations
contained in Chapter-III and desires that the Ministry, in the light of further Recommendations/
Observations of the Committee, furnish explanations thereof.
Chapter IV : The Recommendations/Observations in respect of which the Committee desire further
comments of the Ministry.
In respect of recommendations placed in Chapter-IV , the Ministry has either furnished the
interim replies, therefore, the Committee desires that the Ministry may furnish Action Taken
Notes in respect of recommendations categorized in Chapter-IV in detail and to the point, as
per the intention and spirit of the recommendations of the Committee.
The details of the A TR of the Ministry and Recommendations/Observations of the Committee thereon
are given in the succeeding pages.

CHAPTER-I
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS, WHICH HA VE BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE MINISTRY
Recommendation/Observation
1. The Committee observes that the allocations of the Ministry were either reduced or enhanced at the
R.E. stage, but the actual expenditure incurred most of the time is less than the Revised Estimate. The
Committee is therefore, of the opinion that adequate steps should be taken to monitor the output of
various Schemes, including individual components so that the output targets are achieved timely.
(Para 11)
Action Taken
Ministry has taken measures for improving expenditure. Consequently, the utilization of funds has
been 95.8% during 2017-18 as indicated below:

2. It is observed that the allocation and utilization of funds under the plan schemes of the Ministry
during the last three years have been almost equal. The Committee is of the view that the funds for meeting
the salaries and pensions should be considered suitably without affecting the funds for the development
schemes. The Committee also desires that the Ministry may follow-up with the Ministry of Finance for
release of funds timely. (Para 18)
Action Taken

CHAPTER-II
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS WHICH THE COMMITTEE DOES NOT DESIRE TO
PURSUE FURTHER IN VIEW OF THE GOVERNMENT’S REPLIES
Recommendation/Observation
29. In the opinion of the Committee, most of the MSMEs are not paid timely by the Government
organizations and PSUs for their supply as a result of which MSMEs face serious financial crunch and it
becomes very difficult for them to survive in the market. On the other hand they have to dole out a high rate
of interest to the Banks against their loans for delayed repayment. Further , procurement from SC/ST Enterprises
has also not received adequate attention under the Public Procurement Policy. The Committee recommends
that the Ministry of MS&ME should take immediate measures with the concerned Ministries/Departments to
sort out these issues to dispel the apprehensions of MSME sector. (Para 20)
Action Taken
In order to support the MSEs in overcoming the problem of delayed payments, the Ministry of MSME
has launched MSME - SAMADHAAN portal. MSME units facing problem of delayed payments can register
their complaint directly on this portal. If the matter does not get resolved within 15 days, it automatically
gets transferred to the concerned MSE Facilitation Council. The portal can be accessed by the Heads of
CPSUs/State PSUs/Government Departments.
The Ministry of MSME has also taken following steps to facilitate procurement by CPSEs from MSEs
owned by SC/ST entrepreneurs.
(i) Establishment of National SC/ST Hub, operated by NSIC, which helps in fulfilling the mandate
given to CPSEs and Central Government Departments / Agencies for at least 4% procurement
from SC/ST MSE units.
(ii) Ministry of MSME has launched MSME SAMBANDH portal on 8th December, 2017 with a
view to promoting ease of access to upcoming procurements by CPSE/Govt. Departments.
This has yielded very good results.
(iii) Ministry of MSME has earlier launched Udyog Aadhaar registration to ensure ease in the registration
of enterprises. This registration bears details of category which facilitate easier identification of
SC/ST entrepreneurs.
(iv) S tate level conclaves are being organized across the country by the Ministry. 22 such State
conclaves have already been organised under National SC/ST Hub (NSSH) which were
participated by around 12000 existing/ aspiring SC/ST entrepreneurs.
Concerns relating to delivery of financial services have been shared with the Department of Financial
Services with a request for necessary intervention to be submitted before DRPSCI.
Recommendation/Observation

SMEs, although, resolved to a certain extent by introduction of a few portals for MSME sector, yet, it should
be settled effectively and a time limit for defaulting large Companies be fixed along with some penal
11

12
provisions for making delayed payments to MSME units so that both Large and Small units are enable to

measures like the MSME Samadhaan portal. State Govts. have been requested to further streamline the
functioning of MSEFCs. Regular video conferencing is being held with state governments to expedite the
resolution of cases of delayed payments.
Recommendation/Observation

State/Divisional Directors and their performance is being continuously reviewed. KYIC has introduced MIS
Package to monitor the performance of the training centres and the KYIC has also engaged the services of
Call Centre to get the feedback from the trainees regarding their experience in the training centre.
Recommendation/Observation
39. The recent innovative step to bring in fashion designer of repute to design Khadi fabrics is a welcome
move and it needs to be continued by bringing in more such steps. The Committee therefore recommends that
this along with good market techniques like frequent awareness campaigns among the youth and introduction
of Khadi in Schools. Hospitals and railways could be good recourse which will surely increase the demand
for Khadi products. Along with this, premier showrooms known as Khadi lounge should be opened in all the
States capitals and Airports to market designer Khadi products. (Para 53)

15
Action Taken
KVIC is promoting Khadi among the youth by participating in the events organized by Schools and
Colleges of repute. Moreover, during the exhibitions organized by KVIC, competitions like debate, essay
writing, cultural programmes, drawing competition, fashion show etc are also organized.
There are 26 items under Khadi, which have been registered in the Government e-Marketplace (GeM)
portal for supplies to Govt. Departments, PSUs, Railways etc. Railways are the largest consumer for Khadi
products with annual requirement of `60.00 crore approximately.
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Govt. of India has already issued directives to AIIMS,
NEIGRIHMS, JIPMER, PGI, NIMHANS, RIMS and others for procurement of 45 Khadi and Village Industry
items.
KVIC has opened Khadi Lounge at New Delhi, Mumbai, Jaipur and Bhopal. Exclusive sales outlets at
major airports have also been opened at Visakhapatnam, Ahmedabad and Lucknow. It is also proposed to
open 5 new sales outlets in major airports.
Recommendation/Observation
40. The Committee is of the view that the economic empowerment of the poor artisans can be enhanced by
more intervention by KVIC by allowing the spinners and weavers need to be allowed to work with the
private designers without the approval of KVIC so that they could earn more wages directly from these
designers. (Para 54)
Action Taken
The spinners/weavers are self-employed artisans of Khadi Institutions. There is no restriction by
KVIC on any Khadi Institution and artisans to associate themselves with private designers. Under the KVIC-
Raymond agreement many Khadi Institutions have been encouraged to supply directly, to enable the artisans
to get better wages.
Recommendation/Observation
41. The Committee observes that the urban youths are not inclined to work in this sector due to low wages
and the hardships involved in it. The Committee recommends that the issue of low wages of unskilled, semi
skilled artisans needs to be addressed on priority as the availability of more willing workers will bring in more
quality outcome in Khadi sector . This would help in increasing the benefits to the artisans. (Para 55)
Action Taken
Recently, Ministry of MSME approved a proposal of KYIC to enhance the wages of spinners from
` 5.50 to ` 7.50 per hand to attract more youth to Khadi sector. With the initiatives taken by- KVIC, to
associate the private sector players and setting up of franchisees, it is expected that the youth will be more
attracted to this sector.
Recommendation/Observation
42. The Committee is of the opinion that the minimum educational qualification prescribed under the
PMEGP and absence of the option of regional language in publicity/procedural formality may be the probable
reasons hampering the proper implementation of the flagship scheme as a potential entrepreneur with low

16
education profile may be prone to face difficulties in completion of all procedural formalities including
filling up of form. In this regard, necessary steps should be taken to address the problem. (Para 66)
Action Taken
As regards publicity, the advertisements are published allover the country in regional languages also.
For the filing the online application and procedural formality, the option of English and Hindi language is
available on the e-portal of flagship scheme of Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme
(PMEGP).
To solve the difficulties of potential entrepreneurs in completion of all the procedural formalities
including filling up of form due to low education profile, RUDSETI/RSETI offer handholding services to the
trainees for a period of 2 years to address teething problems if any and to facilitate the sanction of loan and
to ensure that the units are properly grounded.
Recommendation/Observation
43. The Committee also observes that only half the targeted projects set up by KVIC have been approved/
disbursed by the Banks which does not portray a rosy scenario. The Committee desires that the Ministry
may step in to r esolve the problems in consultation with KVIC and financial institutions so that targets set
forth are achieved. (Para 67)
Action Taken
KVlC invites online application under PMEGP scheme. The applications received are placed before the
District Level Task Force Committee (DLTFC). Further, DLTFC takes interview of the candidates and
assess the capability according to type of project to be set up by the entrepreneur. The projects of candidates
recommended by DLTFC are forwarded to the financing banks as per the choice of candidate. The financing
banks assess the techno-economic viability of the projects and sanction the funds according to banking
norms after assessment of the credit profile of the borrowers.
The KVIC and the Ministry hold meetings with the Banks and Nodal officers of Banks on a regular
basis to ensure that the targets are achieved.
Recommendation/Observation
44. The Committee is of the opinion that MSMEs are an integral part of the economic development of the
country and therefore their growth and survival is vital for the Government. Hence, it recommends that more
and more MSME exposition, MSME Haats and MSME National/International trade fairs/Exhibitions should
be organized, including at District level, with the participation of people’s representatives, to enhance the
market accessibility of MSMEs. (Para 91)
Action Taken
Various steps are taken by the Ministry [or MSME to give a better exposure to MSMEs in domestic
and international market for their products/ services. Under the existing Marketing Assistance Scheme and
Special Marketing Assistance Scheme of NSSH, National Small Industries Corporation Ltd. (NSIC) a PSU
under this Mini stry acts as a facilitator to promote marketing efforts and enhance the competency of the
micro, small and medium enterprises for capturing the new market opportunities by way of organizing!
participating in various domestic and international exhibitions/trade fairs, buyer-seller meets, intensive-

17
campaigns and other marketing events. NSIC helps micro and small enterprises to participate in International/
National exhibitions/trade fairs at the subsidized rates to exhibit and market their products. Participation in
the marketing events provides micro, small and medium enterprises an exposure to the National/International
markets.
Further, under International Cooperation Scheme, financial assistance is provided on reimbursement
basis to the State/Central Government organizations, industries/enterprises Associations and registered
societies/trusts and organizations associated with MSME for deputation of MSME business delegation to
other countries for exploring new areas of MSMEs, participation by Indian MSMEs in international exhibitions,
trade fairs, buyer seller meet and for holding international conference and seminars which are in the interest
of MSME sectors.
Recommendation/Observation
45. Deforestation is one of the major threats for the maintenance of ecological balance. The Committee,
in order to avoid grave threats which are endangering the climatic conditions and human life, recommends
that the production of substitutes for wood, such as coir wood, has to be encouraged and more coir
clusters under SFURTI have to be established to meet the demands of coir based furnishings and building
materials from the domestic as well as international market. To achieve this, more funds should be
allocated by the Ministry of MS&ME to the Coir Board with proper monitoring and utilization of allocated
funds. (Para 106)
Action Taken
Against the BE 2017-18 of  `75 crore, an allocation of `125 crore has been earmarked under SUFRTI..
Automatically, the share of Coir Board will be higher than the previous year. Under the Scheme of Fund for
Regeneration of Traditional Industries (SFURTI), the Government of India has sanctioned financial assistance
for establishment of two clusters for production of Needled Felt coir composite panels. Further, Coir Board
has proposed establishment of another cluster in Tamil Nadu viz. Salem, for production of needled felt based
coir composite panels. In addition to this, Coir Board is taking all out efforts to take up new cluster proposals
under SFURTI 2nd Phase exclusively for manufacturing coir wood and related products.
Recommendation/Observation
46. The Committee is of the firm opinion that in order to have a better co-ordination of export promotion
of coir and its by products for aiding in multifarious activities such as soil erosion control, landscaping,
river embankment etc., establishment of overseas offices of the Coir Board may be considered. This way, the
Coir Industry would also grow internationally side by side with the Khadi Industry. (Para 107)
Action Taken
Coir Board is regularly participating in the Annual Conference and Expo of International Erosion
Control Association in America which is a global platform for addressing erosion control issues. Application
of coir geo-textiles in erosion control, landscaping and rural road construction have immense potential
world over because of the eco-friendly nature when compared to synthetic products and other natural
fibers. In order to popularize the use of coir gee-textiles abroad, Coir Board has plans for organizing field
demonstrations on the application of coir gee-textiles and such other initiatives for capturing potential markets
abroad. The proposal for establishing overseas offices has already been included in the future action plans of
the Board. For meeting the expenditure involved the possibilities of convergence with the Market Access

18
Initiative (MAI) scheme of the Ministry of Commerce and the support of the Ministry of External affairs will
be explored.
Recommendation/Observation
47. The Coir Board is implementing multifarious developmental and promotional activities when in
turn is providing employment to a large number of people mostly in the rural areas of the country.
Sufficient manpower is however required for implementation and monitoring the programmes and for
providing research data/statistics in time for MIS. Hence, the Committee recommends that in view of the
increased activities of the Board. the necessary qualified manpower should be provided to the Board for
its smooth functioning. (Para 108)
Action Taken
It is to mention that a High Level Official Committee was constituted for reviewing and assessment of
the direct recruitment vacancies existing in Coir Board, creation of new posts, posts to be provided as
matching savings towards creation/upgradation of posts etc. The Committee, after assessment of the relevant
factors, recommended to impress upon the Ministry the essentiality for immediate filling up of the direct
recruitment vacancies, which include a number of technical posts to be positioned in Field Offices like
Regional Offices/ Sub Regional Offices, through which Plan programmes are implemented and accord
sanction for the same. Similarly, it has also been recommended to follow up the proposal for creation of 20
senior level new posts, already under the consideration of the Ministry, which are also equally important
against the necessity for more effective implementation of the schemes in coir sector with increased budgetary
support.
Recommendation/Observation
48. The Committee is aware that there are various other schemes implemented by the Government under
which technology developed is transferred to the beneficiaries without any charges. The Committee is therefore
is of the view that the technology developed by the Coir Board should be transferred to entrepreneurs,
traders, clusters etc. free of cost to encourage potential entrepreneurs to get into the coir sector. Besides,
steps should also be taken to explore the potential overseas markets for export of coir products particularly
innovative coir products. Also, 100% modernization of coir industry has to be encouraged with high funding
support to popularize the innovative coir products in domestic market as well. (Para 115)
Action Taken
The Government of India has from time to time emphasized the need of its organizations becoming
self-supporting through income generation activities. Earnings through transfer of technology are a source
of income for Coil’ Board. However, free transfer of technology can be considered on a case to case basis
depending on the category of beneficiaries, area of improvement, etc. For instance, technologies that could
improve the productivity of workers, quality of products, etc. could be transferred free of cost. In order to
expand the overseas markets for Indian coir products, the Coir Board is implementing programmes like
participation in international exhibitions and buyer seller meets. Under this programme, the Board undertake
the following activities:
(i) Organise national participation in international fairs abroad.
(ii) Organise participation in international fairs in India.

19
(iii) Organise exclusive international fairs for coir in India and abroad.
(iv) Or ganise Buyer Seller Meets abroad for coir.
(v) Organise reverse Buyer Seller Meets in India.
(vi) Or ganise participation in Seminars, Conferences, Workshops etc. abroad.
(vii) Organise display of coir products in the premises of Indian Missions.
(viii) Undertake demonstrations projects on a pilot scale, conducting seminars etc based on a focus
product/ focus market approach with a view to educate and establish the end use applications of
specific products like coir gee-textiles, coir wood etc. among the target audience.
In addition to the above, the Board is implementing the External Market Development Assistance
scheme with the objective of encouraging the small scale exporters to enter global market and to expand the
export of Indian coir products. Under this scheme, the eligible entrepreneurs will get reimbursement of
space rent, air fare, freight charges, etc. for participation in international exhibitions/buyer seller meets as
per the eligibility conditions and scale of assistance prescribed in the scheme.
Recommendation/Observation
49. The Committee is also of the opinion that Buyer Seller meets and Vendor Development Programmes
may be organized overseas to popularize coir products and to tap the virgin overseas markets. (Para 116)
Action Taken
Ministry of MSME is already organising International Trade Fair to popularize the various product
including coir product and to see the opportunity for marketing of their products.
Recommendation/Observation

` 50 crores
has been made for the first time during 2018-19. Though the Solar Charkha mode will surely remove
drudgery, the Committee is of the view that the KVlC should ensure that there is no conflict in the definition
of Khadi which originally was totally ‘hand spun’, but with the introduction of Solar Charkha, it would

Solar cloth produced out of solar yarn from Solar Charkha has been categorized under Village Industries

Grant-in-Aid General : ` 13.00 crores
SCC : ` 18.00 crores
STC : ` 09.00 crores

NER : ` 10.00 crores
TOTAL : ` 50.00 crores

51. The Committee is of the view that the Ministry of MS&ME should consider other available options to
provide necessary raw materials required by the MSMEs and for this, the other concerned Ministries/
Departments be persuaded for allocation of raw materials like, aluminum, copper, paraffin wax, cement
and bitumen etc. to fulfill the requirement of MSME sector. (Para 140)

In order to provide necessary raw materials required by the MSMEs certain quantities of raw materials
should be allocated by the main producers under Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) with special
discount for distribution to MSMEs through NSIC. Materials like Polymer Products, Bitumen, Copper,
Zinc, Paraffin Wax and Pig Iron should be provided so that MSMEs can be benefitted.

to the prospective entrepreneurs by imparting training in the manufacturing as well as service sector for skill
development. In view of the huge skill demand existing in the country, the Committee recommends that more
Incubation Centres should be established in co-ordination with State Government so that training in
conventional trade as well as hi-tech areas are imparted to entrepreneurs to accure skill in all areas of
business operation for gainful employment. (Para 141)
