11.13 The Committee recommends that as agreed to by both Ministry of MSME and Ministry of
Law and Justice, the amendments in clause (g), (h) & (m) of Section 2 (definition) of the MSMED
Act, 2006 be carried out simultaneously to ensure complete consequential amendment.
11.14 Taking into consideration the views of majority of the stakeholders and the arguments put
forth by the M/o MSME, the Committee feels that instead of the current classification based on
investment in plant & machinery/equipment, the MSMEs could be classified based on their
annual turnover as proposed in the Bill.
General Observations/Recommendations
12.1 With the proposed change in the classification of MSMEs, it is more likely that large
number of Enterprises would come under the Ministry of MSME. The Committee, therefore,
desires that the Ministry may make all-out efforts to obtain increased Budget Allocation for the
MSME Sector. It accordingly desires that the Ministry may take up the issue with Ministry of
Finance in right earnestness.
12.2 To allay the apprehensions of some of the stakeholders, in view of the proposed change in
definition of MSMEs, the Ministry has stated that necessary adjustment to safeguard the interests
of MSEs would be done. The Committee notes the flexibility adduced by the Ministry to make
necessary course corrections in the policy and schemes for incentives to the MSEs, so that they
do not get adversely affected.
12.3 The Committee is of the opinion that there is some weightage in the apprehensions expressed
by the stakeholders as the Committee too feels that possibilities do exist for the large corporates
or the MNCs to corner the incentives meant for the MSMEs, which has in fact, been explicitly
exhibited in the Research Study conducted by the One-Man Committee, wherein the share of
finance gap amongst the three sub-groups of MSMEs in itself is exorbitant. The Committee,
therefore, desires that the Ministry may put in place suitable policy interventions to avert such
situations, which may prove to be catastrophic to the Indian Industry and Economy as a whole.
The Committee hopes that scheme-specific measure to safeguard the MSME Sector wherever
necessary will be taken up soon after provisions of the Bill are made operational.
12.4 The Committee acknowledges the fact that Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises (MSME)
Sector plays a significant role in the growth of Indian Economy. It also provides the 2nd largest
employment next to Agriculture Sector. MSME also contribute enormously to the socio-economic
well-being and progress of our country. It is therefore, imperative to groom and nurture the
MSME sector .

20
12.5 The Committee is unable to fathom the argument adduced by the Ministry that in the case
of employment criteria in the Indian context, there is non-availability of reliable data and that
there is problem of seasonal variance in labour engagement. The Committee feels that in a
labour-intensive country like India, appropriate focus is required to be concentrated on employment
generation and the best and most accurate platform for this is the MSME Sector, which provides
the greatest employment opportunities, next only to the Agricultural Sector. Therefore, the
Committee recommends that the Government should take up the exercise to assess the number
of persons employed in MSME Sector and consider employment too as a criteria while classifying
MSMEs.
12.6 The Committee notes that the turnover as on 01st April of a particular financial year will
be taken as the turnover of that enterprise for the whole financial year. The turnover of some
enterprises may fluctuate depending on their business, which may result in the change of the
classification of the enterprise. The Committee recommends that in order to address the issue,
scheme-specific safeguards should be adopted by the Ministry so that large enterprises do not
grab the benefits meant for MSEs.
12.7 The Committee feels that with the adoption of new criteria, large number of Micro Enterprises
will benefit from various Government schemes. Mor eover, complicated calculations for paperwork
and requirement of certification by CAs or experts would be settled once for all.
12.8 During the examination of MSMED (Amendment) Bill, 2018, the Committee has come
across different views of experts and stakeholders with regard to re-classification of MSMEs
based on their annual turnover instead of the existing investment in plant and machinery/
equipment, as well as consideration of employment along with the annual turnover for re-
classification of MSMEs.
12.9 However, the Committee feels that the definition/classification based on employment criteria
may not help MSMEs to generate more employment as it appears only an enabling provision and
not an instrument in itself to create more employment. The proposed new criterion based on
Turnover will encompass all enterprises with turn over upto ````` 250 crore.

2. At the outset, the Chairman welcomed the Members of the Committee, Secretary, M/o MSME and
officers from the Legislative Department (Ministry of Law & Justice). The Chairman informed about the
referring of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises Development (Amendment) Bill, 2018 by the Hon'ble
Chairman, Rajya Sabha in consultation with the Hon'ble Speaker, Lok Sabha, to this Committee for
examination and report thereon within 3 months. The Chairman then gave a brief introduction of the
proposed Amendment Bill, which seeks to change the criterion of classification of Micro, Small and
Medium Enterprises from the existing criterion of investment in plant and machinery or equipment to a
new criterion based on annual turnover of the enterprises, with a view to promote ease of doing business
and to put in place a non-discretionary and transparent system in alignment with the current economic
scenario of the country.
3. Thereafter, the Chairman invited the Secretary, M/o MSME to apprise the Committee about the need
to introduce the Amendment Bill proposing a change in classification of MSMEs. The Secretary, M/o
MSME explained that as far as the global ranking of Ease of Doing Business is concerned, India has
improved its ranking in the last four years considerably and is now ranked at 77 instaed of 142. Further,
after the implementation of demonetisation and GST, MSMEs are registering under GSTN and are
shifting from informal economic framework to formal economic framework. Therefore, the classfication
criterion required to be made more transparent, objective and non-discretionary. Thereafter, the Secretary
asked his colleague to make a brief Powerpoint presentation about the proposed Amendment Bill.

29
4. A brief presentation was then made by Shri Ram Mohan Mishra, AS & DC. He explained various
problems and hindrances that are being encountered with the present provisions of classifcation of
MSMEs such as difficulty in verification of the MSMEs leading to increased transaction cost, Inspector
Raj etc. Also, it is being regarded as anti-growth, anti-investment and anti-modernisation and the way
out to all these difficulties was to introduce the proposed Amendment Bill, which shall put in place a
transparent, non-discriminatory and online system of verification of MSMEs. It requires no physical
verification at all because the annual turnover data is readily available on GSTN.
5. After the presentation, Secretary, M/o MSME apprised the Committee about the various criteria
prevailing in different countries and the non-feasibility in including employment as criteria due to seasonal
employment variations and various other factors. The Secretary stressed upon the suitability of annual
turnover based criteria for Indian MSMEs.
6. Thereafter, the Members raised queries such as fluctuation in turnover leading to confusion in
classification of the enterprises in which a micro can become small and small can become micro over
a period of time. The Secretary M/o MSME clarified that the turnover data as on 01st April of the
corresponding year shall be taken as bench-mark for classification of enterprises. Majority of the
Members stressed upon including the employment parameter also as one of the criteria besides turnover,
based on the fact that most of the western countries have adopted employment as one of the criteria
for classification of MSMEs.

properly about the enterprise(s). He also apprised the Committee about the difficulties likely to be
encountered in adopting the employment criterion like enterprises refraining to recruit more employees
for fear of losing the benefits meant for micro and small enterprises and complexity involved due to
seasonal nature of many employments. He concluded that the turnover criterion is best suited for the
current scenario, especially after the introduction of GST because it is easy to understand and apply,
easily verifiable, and it also promotes ease of doing business.
4. Sh. S.K. Gagroo from Chamber of Indian Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises too agreed to the
new proposed criterion of shifting from plant and machinery to the annual turnover-based criteria and
also with the views expressed by Dr. H.P. Kumar about the suitability of the proposed annual turnover
criterion, especially after the introduction of GST, which made the verification of MSMEs simpler and
easier. About changing the current turnover limits, he said that this would be the best method and is in
line with Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code. He further added that under the present investment criteria,
enterprises were incentivised not to invest in plant and machinery for fear of losing the benefits and
remain in the same bracket but under the turnover criterion, enterprises would be encouraged to invest
in plant and machinery and upgrade them to become more competitive. The new criteria will also
promote transparency and easy verification of enterprises. Further, he said that employment criterion will
disincentivise the labour-intensive industries.
5. Thereafter, Members made suggestions for considering employment as one of the criteria besides
turnover, on variable basis like the models of western countries as the MSME Sector is meant for

between the turnover limits for Micro and Small enterprises and therefore suggested for bringing down
the upper limit of turnover of Small Industries to ` 50 crores as against the suggested limit of ` 75 crore

generation to ensure social justice and in larger public interest.

STATEMENT OF OBJECTS AND REASONS
The Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act,
2006 (the said Act) was enacted to provide for facilitating the
promotion and development and enhancing the competitiveness of
micro, small and medium enterprises. The said Act, inter alia, provides
for classification of the enterprises as micro, small or medium based
on their investment in plant and machinery or equipment. Over a
period of time, it has been felt necessary to change the criteria for
the classification in order to align it with the need of current times
and changing business ecosystem.
2. In the course of consultation with various stakeholders, it has
been noted that the criterion of investment in plant and machinery
or equipment entails physical verification having associated transaction
costs. It also incentivises the tendency in the promoters of the
enterprises to keep the investment size small in a particular business
entity in order to retain the benefits associated with micro or small
enterprises category. While evaluating various alternatives, it has
been considered appropriate that if the annual turnover is taken as
a criterion for classification, the information available with goods
and services tax network and other sources can be used for
determination of the category of the enterprises. Overall, the turnover
based clasification will promote the ease of doing business and will
put in place a non-discretionary, transparent and objective classification
system.
3. In view of the above, it is proposed to amend section 7 of the
Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act, 2006 to—
(a) provide for change in the criterion of classification of
micro, small and medium enterprises from the existing
criterion of investment in plant and machinery or equipment
to a new criterion based on annual turnover of the
enterprises; and
(b) confer power upon the Central Government to vary, the
turnover limits, by notification which shall not exceed
thrice the limits specified in sub-section (1) of section 7
for the purpose of development of micro, small and medium
enterprises.
4. The Bill seeks to achieve the above objects.

Gratefully noted.
Recommendation/Observation
3. The Committee is of the considered view that taking into account the rate of inflation, the M/o MSME
should gradually consider to enhance the limit of subsidy i.e., from 
` 15 lakh to ` 25 Lakh in prescribed
sectors / sub-sectors which would prove to be more helpful for MSEs to cater to their needs for up-gradation
of machinery and plants. (Para 33)
Action Taken
It may be mentioned that the thrust of the scheme is also for adequate coverage of the number of
beneficiaries along with reasonable subsidy per unit to be given within over all budgetary limits.  However,
the suggestion of the Committee has been noted for future review.
Recommendation/Observation
4. The Committee, therefore, is of the view that serious efforts with practical approach and result-
oriented goals should be made to dispel the confusion and lack of awareness  about  the scheme in  MSE
Sector  as well as  among  the PLIs  and   Financial Institutes. Technology Exhibitions may be one of the
measures to create awareness. However, there must be a unified attempt by the Ministry of MS&ME and
different Industrial Associations to create awareness among the MSEs about the Schemes. The M/o MSME
should make all out efforts for the growth of the MSEs on a uniform pattern across the country for the
overall development resulting in creation of various job opportunities for the masses and dispelling the
geographical imbalance of industrial set up. Therefore, there is a need of continuance of the scheme for a
longer period. (Para 42)
2

3
Action Taken
In addition to awareness programmes, provisions for Regional/ State/ National Workshops have been
proposed in the revised scheme under which the suggested activities shall be undertaken.  The scheme is
being continued.
Recommendation/Observation
5. The Committee observes that to popularize the CLCS Scheme it should be discussed at appropriate
levels i.e. SLBC, Districts Heads, DIC, Industry Associations and grass-root level etc. for better off take
under the scheme. (Para 43)
Action Taken
In addition to awareness programmes, provisions for Regional/ State/ National Workshops have been
proposed in the revised scheme under which the suggested activities shall be undertaken. The scheme is
being continued.
Recommendation/Observation
6.  The Committee desires that M/o MSME may pursue the matter and the Committee may be apprised as
soon as Cabinet approval is accorded. (Para 48)
Action Taken
Noted for compliance. As soon as cabinet approval is obtained, the same will be intimated to the
Committee for kind perusal.
Recommendation/Observation
7.  The Committee desires that it may be apprised of as soon as norms of the Scheme are revised.
(Para 54)
Action Taken
Noted for compliance. As soon as cabinet approval is obtained, the norms will be finalized and informed
to the committee.
Recommendation/Observation
8.  The Committee is of the opinion that to provide smooth corridor for the betterment of MSEs for
having a flourishing business, there is always a need for concerted efforts at every level. On the whole, the
Committee feels that though measures have been taken for overall development of Industrial sector, yet
there is a lot more to be done for making a New India. (Para 62)
Action Taken
Gratefully noted.

CHAPTER-II
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS  WHICH  THE  COMMITTEE DOES  NOT
DESIRE  TO  PURSUE  IN  VIEW  OF  THE  GOVERNMENT’S  REPLIES
Recommendation/Observation
9. Further , the Committee desires that Ministry of MSME should work in tandem with the State
Governments of the more populous States, where there is less off take of the CLCSS to encourage more and
more promising entrepreneurs to set up industries and also to take part in the Scheme for technical up-
gradation. (Para 23)
Action Taken
The Scheme guidelines have been amended to include awareness programmes across the country
among the prospective and existing entrepreneurs to increase off-take. In organising further awareness
programmes, different stakeholders including the State Governments will also be actively involved particularly
where there is less off-take under the CLCSS.
Recommendation/Observation
10.  The Committee after hearing the Ministry of MSME is of the view that M/o MSME taking the
practical aspect into consideration may ensure or ascertain the genuineness of the claim by MSEs for
subsidy against the purchase of machines or requirement of the machines for technology up-gradation, the
M/o MSME may consider about the possibility of a Third Party Evaluation by some rating agency or NSIC
or SIDBI who can report directly to the M/o MSME in this regard and thereafter the Ministry may take
necessary action without delaying the process. (Para 35)
Action Taken
In the present system, due diligence is done by the bank itself before sanctioning the term loan for
procurement of machines by the unit. Due diligence is also carried out by the bank before approval of the
subsidy at their end. The involvement of third party evaluation is therefore, not likely to add any value in the
process of ensuring or ascertaining the genuineness of the claim by MSE and may in fact, delay the process.
However, the Ministry would get an evaluation of the scheme done by a third party for future improvement
in service delivery.
Recommendation/Observation
11.  The Committee observes that less intake under CLCSS in NER perhaps due to the existence of the
NEIP scheme offering more subsidy vis-a-vis CLCSS. (Para 36)
Action Taken
The North East Industrial Development Scheme (NEIDS), 2017 has a component of Central Capital
Investment Incentive for Access to Credit (CCIIAC) which provides subsidy @ 30% of the investment in
Plant and Machinery with an upper limit of ` 5.00 Cr. on the incentive amount per unit.
Recommendation/Observation
12.  The Committee accordingly desires that Ministry may chalk out measures to make the CLCSS more
attractive by perhaps increasing the subsidy in order to woo the NE entrepreneurs. (Para 37)
4

5
Action Taken
In order to attract the NE entrepreneurs, the Ministry has already incorporated necessary measures in
the revised scheme. The subsidy shall now not be restricted to the identified technologies/sectors in NER
but shall be admissible also for investments for acquisition/replacement of plant and machinery/equipments
and technology up-gradation of any kind, except second hand machinery/equipment for NE entrepreneurs.
Recommendation/Observation
13.  The Committee was of the view that when a woman entrepreneur is eligible in any sector, the benefit
of subsidy should be credited to her individual account or account of the enterprise, as the case may be
without any delay. The subsidy should be extended as margin money rather than granting it at the completion
of 3 years. (Para 45)
Action Taken
The Ministry has provision for women entrepreneurs for extending the benefits of the Scheme.
Further, in order to ensure fair inclusion of women entrepreneurs, the subsidy shall be admissible also
for investment in acquisition/replacement of plant and machinery/equipments and technology up-gradation
of any kind irrespective of the fact whether the sector/technology is listed within the identified sectors/
technologies under the Scheme.
Further, on receipt of the subsidy, the bank reduces the outstanding loan to the unit by the amount of
the subsidy. Consequently, the unit is getting a proportionate benefit throughout debt servicing period, from
inception to the end.
Recommendation/Observation
14. The Committee is of the opinion that if the SMEs are shifted from their present location on the plea of
energy or environmental pollution, adequate infrastructural facility viz. Power, road, easy labour etc. should
be provided to them before shifting them. (Para 47)
Action Taken
Noted. However, the suggestion is beyond the scope of the Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme.
Recommendation/Observation
15. The Committee is of the considered opinion that besides Technology up-gradation before granting
subsidy the basic difficulties being faced by the MSEs viz, land, power, water, communication and road
facilities etc. should also be taken care of appropriately to make the MSEs globally competitive and grow in
a hindrance free environment. (Para 50)
Action Taken
MSE Cluster Development Programme of Ministry of MSME is helping MSEs in respect of land,
power, water, communication and road facilities etc.
Recommendation/Observation
16. The Committee is of the view that subsidy should be released to MSEs in such cases where the delay in
submission of cases occurs on the part of PLIs and Nodal Agency. Further, the Ministry should develop an

6
online mechanism to monitor the applications and identify whether delay occurred on the part of MSEs or
banks. (Para 59)
Action Taken
An online monitoring system has already been put in place and will be modified further to keep check
on such cases.
Recommendation/Observation
17. In the opinion of the Committee, the Ministry may consider setting up of a Grievance Committee or an
Ombudsman to oversee all aspects of the Scheme and where an aggrieved entrepreneur could turn too to
make his grievances/problems heard for resolution thereof. Alternatively they may consider setting up of a
web portal to review feedbacks/grievances regarding the scheme and other related problems pertaining to
MSME Sectors. (Para 63)
Action Taken
In addition to the common Central Government Grievance Redressal Mechanism i.e. CPGRAM, the
Ministry has its own Internet Grievance Monitoring System (IGMS) to address and review feedbacks/
grievances regarding the scheme and other related problems pertaining to the MSME Sector.

CHAPTER-III
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS  IN  RESPECT  OF  WHICH  THE  COMMITTEE
HAS  NOT  ACCEPTED  THE  REPLIES  OF  THE  MINISTRY  AND  DESIRES
THE  MINISTRY  TO  REVIEW  THEIR  REPLIES
Recommendation/Observation
18. The Committee desires that the outcome of such visits may be disclosed to the Committee and whether
the visits have had any lasting impact on percolating the benefits of the Scheme to the grass root levels in
these aspirational Districts or not. (Para 22)
Action Taken
Teams of officers including the officials from our field setup have visited 115 Aspirational districts to
enable the benefit of the Scheme reaching the grass roots. Ministry is working on the recommendations of
these teams.
Further Recommendation/Observation
The Committee may be informed of the outcomes, if any, of these visits to the Aspirational
Districts so far.  The Committee may also be informed whether these visits have been able to create
awareness and increased outreach about the scheme among the entrepreneurs.  Further, the
Committee would like to know the details of recommendations that have been made by these teams
who visited the 115 Aspirational Districts and any noticeable change in the off-take of the Scheme
after these visits.
Recommendation/Observation
19. The Committee recommends that the timeline for application process and disbursement of subsidy
should be reduced by the M/o MSME by co-ordinated effort with the Department of Financial Services.
(Para 49)
Action Taken
In case of availability of sufficient budgetary provision, the timeline for application process and
disbursement of subsidy shall automatically be reduced.
Further Recommendation/Observation
The Committee is of the view that the Ministry should approach the M/o Finance for sufficient
Budgetary allocation under the CLCS Scheme to ensure timely disbursement of subsidy to the
beneficiaries of MSEs.
Recommendation/Observation
20.  The Committee therefore, is of the view that M/o MSME should approach the M/o Finance for
diversion of allocated budget from other schemes and allocate this fund for benefit of Micro and Small
Enterprises under CLCSS at last quarter of the financial year. The Committee also feels that delays in
release of budget under the scheme delay the process of disbursement of subsidy which should be taken up
with M/o Finance for timely allocation. (Para 55)
7

8
Action Taken
Ministry has sought budget under supplementary demand from Ministry of Finance in order to liquidate
pending liabilities under the scheme during the current FY itself.
Further Recommendation/Observation
The Committee notes that delay in disbursement of subsidy discourages the entrepreneurs
and adversely affects the MSEs and ultimately economic growth and employment generation of the
country.  The Committee, therefore, is of the view that the Ministry should pursue the matter with
the M/o Finance for sufficient Budget allocation so that subsidy could be disbursed to SMEs on
time-bound basis avoiding pending liabilities.

CHAPTER-IV
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS  IN  RESPECT  OF  WHICH  THE  COMMITTEE
DESIRE  FURTHER  COMMENTS  OF  THE  MINISTRY
Recommendation/Observation
21. The Committee is of the opinion that the Ministry of MSME has to ensure that in future, appropriate
measures should be taken for induction of more sectors/sub-sector/technologies under the CLCS scheme in
addition to the existing 51 Sectors/sub-sectors/technologies for all categories of entrepreneurs.
(Para 28)
Action Taken
The Scheme Guidelines are being amended to make the list of technologies/machines eligible for
subsidy dynamic with provision for updation and deletion of the technologies/machines based on emerging
requirement of the entrepreneurs.
Recommendation/Observation
22.  The Committee is of the opinion that the CLCS Scheme should be made applicable for all sectors
(including plant and machinery) for subsidy under CLCSS. The Committee, therefore is of the view that the
M/o MS&ME should also ask the Ministry of Finance for more budgetary allocation for betterment of MSE
sector as well as liquidate pending liabilities under the scheme. (Para 29)
Action Taken
Ministry has sought budget in the supplementary demand from Ministry of Finance. The additional
budgetary allocation will liquidate all pending liabilities under the scheme during the current FY itself.
Recommendation/Observation
23.  The Committee is of the view that the Ministry of MSME should regularly monitor the progress in the
matter in co-ordination with State Governments so that the Scheme reaches out to more entrepreneurs. The
Committee also suggests that subsidy for women entrepreneurs of all categories should be raised to 25
percent as is the case of SC/ST entrepreneurs after exploring the feasibility. (Para 38)
Action Taken
To make the CLCSS more attractive for women entrepreneurs, a provision has been proposed under
which the subsidy shall be admissible also for investment in acquisition/replacement of plant and machinery/
equipments and technology up-gradation of any kind, except second hand machinery/equipment. The subsidy
is being retained @15% up to ` 15.00 Lakh in all cases including SC/ST enterprises. However, a Special
CLCSS under National SC/ST Hub Scheme has been launched, which will provide 25% subsidy to SC/ST
entrepreneurs.
Recommendation/Observation
24. The Committee is of the opinion that the Ministry of MSME should conduct a study in all states to
know as to how the awareness could be created to get the optimum out of the Scheme. The Ministry may also
undertake a research study to know the reason as to how five States achieved a stupendous target of 77%
while the rest of India lagged behind. (Para 52)
9

10
Action Taken
In organising the awareness programmes, stakeholders including the State Governments will also be
involved particularly where the off- take under the scheme has lagged behind. Moreover, removal of sectoral
limitations and inclusion of provisions for special categories including SC/ST category, women entrepreneurs
and  entrepreneurs from NER, Hill states (Jammu & Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand) island
territories (Andaman & Nicobar and Lakshadweep) and the identified Aspirational Districts/ LWE Districts
will help to encourage the more promising entrepreneurs, particularly in the States with low off take. The
reason for better performance five states appears to be their high industrial base and consequent higher
demand.
