disbursement under ISEC is Rs. 40.00 crore to 1370 Khadi Institutions (up to 31 - 03 - 2021). 
Also it has been  observed by the Committee from the status of ISEC claim for the FY 2020 -21 
that the scheme is not performing satisfactorily in the states of Haryana,  Chhattisgarh, Assam, 
Orissa, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Telengana and Karnataka (DO Hubli). It was informed by the 
Ministry that the probable reasons for underperformance in availing the ISEC Scheme could be 

22

Committee (SLBC) and Block Level Bankers' Committee (BLBC) in the respective states. KVIC 
is also organizing awareness programme with bankers to make them aware of the ISEC Scheme 
and Khadi Programme.

Scheme of Fund for Regeneration of Traditional Industries (SFURTI)  
50. The Committee was informed by the Ministry that Government of India has launched 
the Scheme of Fund for Regeneration of Traditional Industries (SFURTI) with an aim to 
organize the traditional artisan s into clusters and to make the Traditional Industries more 
productive, profitable and capable for generating sustained employment. Under the scheme, the 
clusters are provided with assistance in setting up Common Facility Centers, Raw Material 
Banks, procurement of machines, training, exposure visits, branding etc. Maximum support from 
Government of India under the scheme is up to Rs. 5 crore for a cluster of more than 500 artisans 
and up to Rs. 2.5 crore for up to 500 artisans.  
51. It was also informed that the Ministry of MSME have approved 335 proposals for 
setting up clusters under the scheme benefitting around 1.98 lakh artisans and approved an 
amount of Rs.784.85 crores as Government of India grant for implementation of clusters  since 
2015-16 to 2020-21 (till 31.12.2020). 79 clusters have become functional till 31.12.2020. These 
clusters are in Khadi, Coir, Handicraft, Handloom, Agro -processing, honey sector etc.  In 2020 -
21, 37 clusters have been approved till 31.12.2020 assisti ng 21,226 artisans. Ministry has 
released an amount of Rs. 127.41 cr. during the year 2020-21 (till 31.12.2020) for implementing 
the activities prescribed in the DPRs such as setting up of Common Facility Centres (CFC), 
procurement of machineries, conducti ng Soft Interventions activities such as marketing 
initiatives, awareness programmes etc.  

24 
 
52. Further, the Committee was informed that 371 clusters have been approved till now and 
only 82 clusters are operational under SFURTI Scheme. The Ministry submitte d that SFURTI is 
an excellent scheme targeted at the welfare of artisans across the farthest areas of the country and 
assured to give prominence to this Scheme.  Besides, the Ministry informed that normally setting 
up of clusters was taking around three years but now it is taking around one plus year. 
53. The Committee notes that the BE for SFURTI Scheme for FY 2020-21 i.e. Rs. 464.85 
crore was reduced at the RE Stage to Rs. 300 crore and the Actual Expenditure was only 
Rs. 192.54 crores till 31 st January, 2021. The Committee also notes that against a projected 
Budget Estimate of Rs. 500 crore for the SFRUTI Scheme for FY 2021 -2022, an allocation 
of only Rs. 170 crore has been made. The Committee expresses its concern over the low 
utilization pattern and red uction in allocations for an important Scheme of the Ministry, 
which is capable of generating employment in a large scale in the rural areas for the 
artisans, particularly during the Covid Pandemic. The Committee recommends that a 
holistic evaluation study of the Scheme may be conducted and based on the said study more 
allocations should be projected by the Ministry at the RE Stage for effective 
implementation of SFURTI Scheme for benefit of the traditional artisans. 
54. The Committee is constrained to note that out of 371 clusters which have been 
approved, only 82 clusters are operational so far. The Committee recommends that the 
process of setting up of SFURTI clusters should be expedited; targets should be set and 
ensure that the approved clusters are completed and become operational within the 
stipulated timeframe for benefit of artisans.   
55. The Committee was apprised by the Ministry that besides 219 Districts, 56 
Aspirational Districts have also been covered under S FURTI. The Committee recommends 
that more attention should be paid to target more and more Aspirational Districts across 
the country as this can immensely improve the socio-economic conditions of the inhabitants 
in those districts and improve the human dev elopment index. The Ministry may coordinate 
with the state governments and with concerted efforts desired results may be achieved.  
56. During the Covid Pandemic induced lockdowns, scores of migrant workers were 
forced to return to their native places and had to stay back for months without any 
livelihood/ employment.  SFURTI is one such Scheme which has the potential to generate 
employment in rural areas with less investment for the artisans. The Committee 

25 
 
recommends that Ministry should endeavour to set u p more SFURTI clusters and ensure 
that each and every district of the country has SFURTI clusters on the lines of one -district 
one-product to solve the problem of unemployment in rural areas.

Covid Pandemic and MSME Sector 
 
91. The COVID -19 spread very fast to almost all the countries of the world  and on  11th 
March, 2020, the World Health Organization (WHO) declared it as a Pandemic. In India, the first 
COVID-19 case was reported from Kerala on 30th January, 2020, and subsequently the Pandemic 
spread to almost all the States/UTs. In order to contain the spread of COVID -19 Pandemic, the 
Government of India took various steps such as enforcing social distancing norms, self -isolation 
measures, travel ban, border closure and lockdown of the entire country. 
92. The Pandemic has significantly hampered economic activity all across the world. The 
restricted movement due to lockdown had severe effect on all the sectors of the economy 
especially on the MSMEs  in India . Most of them did not have the capacity to deal with 
something so unexpected and unprecedented. Consequently MSMEs, which rely m ostly on the 
cash availability and informal employment , had to face problems such as sudden dip in or ders 
and cash flows, uncertainty in demand, labour related issues , supply chain disruption etc. 
Particularly the Micro E enterprises that comprised the majority of MSME s suffered massive 
losses due to the lockdowns because they had to run their businesses with only limited resources. 

36 
 
A large number of MSMEs comprising manufacturing and service/retail firms had to shut down 
their business es during nationwide lockdowns due to the disruptions in the supply chain as 
procurement of raw materials at affordable rates became very difficult.  
 
Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyaan 
93. Taking cognizance of the gravity of the situation, the Government announced a series of 
measures under the Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyaan  for ameliorating the MSME s. The 
announcements were focused on various important aspects such as availability of credit, demand 
generation, grievance redressal and handholding of MSMEs etc. The steps inter-alia includes: 
 
(i) The Government has notified composite criteria of classification of MSMEs based on 
Investment in plant & machinery or equipment and Turnover of MSMEs as structural 
change to facilitate both existing as well as new entrepreneurs.  
 
(ii) Earlier process of filing  of Udyog Aaadhar  Memorandum has been replaced by 
Udyam Registration  on a Portal developed by the Ministry of MSME, which  is 
expected to bring about many benefits for the MSMEs to grow in size.  
 
(iii) Financial support to the stressed MSMEs with infusion of Rs. 20,000 crore equity 
support through Subordinate Debt which is likely to benefit more than 2 lakh 
MSMEs. 
 
(iv) Fund of Funds created to infuse equity worth Rs.50,  000 crore in the MSME Sector.  
A Rs.10, 000 crore Corpus Fund to be set up which  would provide equity funding to 
growth potential and viable MSMEs. 
 
(v) Regarding e nsuring timely payment to the MSMEs, the Government of India and 
CPSEs have to clear all receivables of MSMEs within 45 days under the Public 
Procurement Policy which will ease  the liquidity problem of MSMEs.  Besides, 
initiatives have been taken for monitoring settlement of dues of MSMEs by larger 
units (Public and Private) through online SAMADHAN and SAMBANDH Portals. 
 
(vi) Rs. 3 lakh crore collateral free automatic loans for business, including MSMEs. 
 
(vii) Global tender to be disallowed in Government procurement Tenders up  to Rs 200 
crores which will provide more market opportunities to domestic entities.

24thJune, 2020. As on 03.02.2021, a total number of 34 Banks have registered as Member

30.84 crore. The objective of the scheme is to provide personal loan through banks to the 
promoters of stressed MSMEs for infusion as equity/quasi equity in the business and provides 
Sub-Debt support in respect of restructuring of MSMEs. The salient features of the Scheme 
are as under: 
(i)   it provides for Rs. 20.000 crore as subordinate debt for Stressed MSMEs. 
(ii) MSME entrepreneurs of such stressed units find it difficult to bring in this additional 
equity and that in turn severely constrains the survival of these units. 

38

brink of becoming NPA.

debt) or Rs. 75 lakh whichever is lower, Promoter(s) in turn will infuse this amount in the 
MSME unit as equity and thereby enhance the liquidity and maintain debt-equity ratio. 
(v)  90% guarantee coverage for this sub-debt will be given under the scheme and 10% would 
come from the concerned Promoters. 
(vi)  There will be a moratorium of 7 years on payment of principal whereas maximum tenure 
for repayment will be 10 years. 
(vii)  Till date, 34 Banks including all PSU Banks have come on-board by signing MoU with 
CGTMSE for becoming the Member Lending Institution (MLI) of the Scheme.

indigenous components for Corona Testing Equipment, hot tape sealing (critical operation for 
PPE coveralls), masks, coveralls, WHO quality alcohol based s anitizers, sanitizer pumps, face 
shields, etc. Besides they have developed UV Disinfector Tower and prototype of Non 
Invasive CPAP type Ventilator.  
 106. Further, the Ministry has provided the following support for import substitution to the 
Industry during 2020-21: 
(i)  CTTC (Bhubaneswar) has developed & manufactured various parts like Crimping

42 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE – AT A GLANCE 
 
1. The Committee hopes that the new classification of MSMEs would bring about 
positive changes in the MSME Sector. The Committee therefore, recommends that a study 
needs to be conducted to know the exact impact of COVID -19 Pandemic on the MSME 
Sector and to ascertain what benefits have accrued to the MSME Sector by change of 
criteria for classification of MSMEs and introduction of various Schemes. The Committee 
may also be apprised about the findings of the study for perusal. 
                   (Para 3) 
 
2. The Committee reiterates its recommendation contained in its 297 th Report that the 
growth of MSMEs is concentrated mostly in a few States only which induces the people to 
migrate to those areas  in search of employment and livelihood. Therefore, the Ministry 
should work in the direction of removing all the existing geographical imbalances and 
ensure that equitable presence of MSMEs is there in all the States so that there is 
horizontal industrialization and adequate employment generation to tide over the situation 
created particularly due to COVID-19 Pandemic.  
                   (Para 4) 
 
3. The Committee observes that the allocations of the Ministry were either reduced or 
enhanced at the R.E. stage, but the actual expenditure incurred most of the time is less than 
the Revised Estimate. The Committee is therefore, of the opinion that proper es timation 
should be done by the Ministry beforehand to ensure that budget is utilized optimally as 
far as possible. The Ministry should also monitor the output of its various Schemes, 
including individual components so that the output targets are achieved timely.   
(Para 11) 
 
4. The Budget Estimate for FY 2021-22 is Rs. 15699.65 crore, which seems a significant 
increase vis-à-vis FY 2020-21. However, out of this amount an allocation of Rs. 10,000 crore 
has been earmarked for the Guaranteed Emergency Credit L ine Scheme (GECL) and in 
effect Rs. 5699.65 crore is the actual allocation, which is a reduction from the BE of FY 
202021. The Committee is worried that in absence of adequate funds how the Ministry is 
planning to implement its various schemes effectively in the present scenario of COVID -19 
Pandemic when MSME Sector is starved of funds. The Committee, therefore, recommends 
that the Ministry may ask for an enhanced allocation at the RE Stage for proper 
implementation of its flagship Schemes and strengthening of the MSME Sector.   
(Para 12) 
 
5. The Committee is also of the opinion that the details of the action plan regarding the 
utilization of funds allocated under GECL Scheme should be worked out and furnished to 
the Committee for perusal. 
(Para 13) 
 
6. The Committee observes that the Ministry could utilize only 66% of the RE for the 
FY 2020-21 (up to January, 2021), which is a cause of concern. However, the Ministry cited 
COVID-19 Pandemic as the main reason for the underutilization of allocated funds. On th e 

43 
 
other hand, the Committee is of the opinion that the budget utilization should have been 
more because of the demand created due to COVID -19 Pandemic in the MSME Sector.  
The Committee is of the opinion that MSME Sector presently is in desperate need of fu nds. 
Therefore, the Ministry must ensure that the allocated budget is utilized optimally so that 
MSME Sector may thrive. 
(Para 15) 
 
7. The Committee notes that up to the end of 3 rd quarter of FY 2020 -21, the Ministry 
could utilize only 54% of the actual budget allocation i.e. Rs. 5664.22 crore. The Committee 
is constrained to note the underutilization of allocated funds and  would like to know the 
reasons for continuously projecting inflated demands and thereafter underutilizing the 
funds. The Committee therefore, recommends that proper assessment and planning should 
be made beforehand in respect of utilization of funds quarter -wise so that there is no rush 
to spend more in the last quarters of the year. 
(Para 17) 
 
8. The Committee is of the view that KVIC should concentrate more on its technology 
improvement and products upgradation aspect in this age of stiff competition with big 
market players. The Committee, therefore, recommends that latest training programmes 
by experienced and experts having expertise  in the field should be imparted to the artisans 
through its network of training institutions for product design and quality improvement in 
order to promote export of Khadi products. Further, the Committee recommends that the 
process of revamping and reori entation of KVIs should also be done wherever required so 
that it helps in productivity development of Khadi and Village Industries. 
(Para 23) 
 
9. The Committee raised concern over difference in BE i.e. Rs. 905 crore for FY 2021 -
22 vis-à-vis BE for FY 2020 -21 i.e. Rs. 1525 crore for Khadi Sector as this being an 
important sector which generates large scale employment for rural people. The Committee 
recommends that considering the importance of Khadi Sector and its employment 
generating potential, an increased budget allocation should be asked for at RE stage by the 
Ministry.  
(Para 24) 
 
10. Recently Khadi Prakritik Paint  has been developed and launched by Khadi and Village 
Industries Commission. The paint is said to be cow dung based, eco -friendly, non-toxic product 
with anti -fungal, anti -bacterial properties. It is claimed that the paint is cost -effective and 
odorless and has been certified by Bureau of Indian Standards. The Committee appreciates the 
efforts made by the KVIC and recommends tha t such type of initiatives and innovations 
take place regularly with the combination of innovative ideas and latest technology. The  
Committee therefore, recommends that adequate funds should be allocated for R&D and 
Technology related support facilities in order to improve the quality of Khadi products vis-
a-vis international products. 
(Para 25) 
 

44 
 
11. The Committee appreciates the effort made by the Ministr y in respect of creating e -
market linkages for strengthening the MSME Sector and recommends that the Ministry 
should analyze the marketing system of MSMEs of developed countries and their system of 
newer technology adoption for their development and adopt the best practices followed 
internationally for advancement and development of indigenous MSMEs.  
(Para 28) 
 
12. The Committee appreciates the efforts made by the Ministry in providing financial 
help to Khadi artisans during Covid Pandemic through Artisan Welfare Fund Trust.  The 
Committee recommends that some kind of contingent fund or financial provision should be 
put in place by the Ministry keeping in view the welfare of the artisans associated with 
MSME Sector for the unforeseen situations like Covid P andemic as a social security 
measure so that some kind of monetary help can be provided to artisans in times of distress 
in future.  
(Para 31) 
 
13. PMEGP is one of the flagship Schemes of the Ministry of MSME which is capable of 
generating large-scale employment for youth of the country, particularly during the Covid 
Pandemic. The Committee however finds that an amount Rs. 2000 crore has been allocate d 
for the Scheme for FY 2021 -2022 vis-à-vis allocation of Rs. 2500 crores during 2020 -2021. 
The Committee recommends that more allocations should be demanded by the Ministry at 
the RE stage for effective implementation of the Scheme. 
(Para 37) 
 
14. The Com mittee is concerned to note that out of the total number of applications 
received under the Scheme, around 76% were forwarded to the banks, only 16% of the 
applications got sanctioned by the banks and a meager 10% of applications got 
disbursements by the b anks. Since PMEGP Scheme is one of the flagship Schemes of the 
Ministry, the Committee recommends that the Ministry should look into the matter and 
take steps for removing the hindrances and simplifying the procedures with minimal 
formalities and technical ities so as to ensure that  off take of loan under the scheme is 
improved. 
(Para 38) 
 
15. The Committee notes that there is huge difference between Margin Money 
allocation and Margin Money utilization in NER.  Also the number of units assisted are 
very few. Employment generation is also negligible. The Committee recommends that more 
clusters/LBIs/TBIs should be set up by the Ministry in NER to overcome the problems of 
unemployment, poverty, drudgery and migration. The Committee also recommends that 
massive awareness programmes should also be organized by the Ministry in NER to create 
awareness a mong people in NER regarding various beneficial programmes/schemes 
implemented by the Ministry.  
(Para 39) 
 
16. During the course of discussion on the DFG (2021 -2022), the Committee observes 
that the constraints faced by KVIC/KVIB are due to procedural del ays, inadequate 

45 
 
technology up -gradation, underutilization of funds etc. Despite providing technical 
guidance to the units in KVI, the problems of the units remain inadequately addressed, as a 
result there is suboptimal functioning of institutions/units and  high drop outs among new 
entrants and low employment generation.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that 
KVIC should come forward with a more pragmatic approach in coordination with all the 
stakeholders. Proper planning, monitoring and implementation of each scheme are 
required to meet the primary objective of employ ment generation, particularly to counter 
COVID-19 Pandemic like situations in future.  
(Para 41) 
 
17. The Committee is of the view that the youths in urban as well as rural areas are not 
inclined to work in KVI Sector due to low wages and the hardships inv olved in it.  
Therefore, the Committee desires that the economic empowerment of the poor artisans can 
be enhanced by allowing the potential artisans (spinners and weavers) to work with the 
private Designer Houses of national and international reputation wit hout the approval of 
KVIC so that they could earn more wages from them directly.  
(Para 42) 
 
18. The Committee observes that Schemes like ISEC, PMEGP etc. of the Ministry are 
not working satisfactorily in North Eastern Region and has a very negligible pres ence in 
the NER.  Even the implementation of the Strengthening of Infrastructure of Existing 
Weak Khadi Institution Scheme is not encouraging. The Committee recommends that 
initiatives should be taken by the Ministry for revival of weak Khadi Institutions with the 
help of State Governments in the NER, which has a vigorous craft tradition and manifests 
itself in its various products from cane and bamboo handicrafts to metalwork and gorgeous 
textiles. 
(Para 43) 
 
19. The Committee observes that the ISEC issued  and bank finance provided to the 
Institutions is not very encouraging, mainly due to the existence of problems like lack of 
awareness among the people or some kind of procedural hassles. The Committee therefore, 
recommends that adequate steps should be ta ken by the Ministry to organize awareness 
programs and utilise social media to popularize the Scheme. To increase the off take, the 
procedures may be simplified, formalities may be kept at minimum, and banks may be 
educated about the Scheme and advised to adopt friendly and favourable approach while 
considering the applications and claims. 
(Para 48) 
 
20. The Committee observes that the ISEC issued and the amount disbursed to the 
Khadi Institutions in the North Eastern Regions is not very encouraging. The Co mmittee 
therefore, recommends that reasons responsible for underperformance of the Scheme 
should be ascertained and informed to the Committee for perusal.  Remedial measures 
should also be taken by the Ministry for improving the off take of the Scheme in N ER 
which is lagging behind in comparison to other states of the country. 
(Para 49) 
 

46 
 
21. The Committee notes that the BE for SFURTI Scheme for FY 2020-21 i.e. Rs. 464.85 
crore was reduced at the RE Stage to Rs. 300 crore and the Actual Expenditure was only 
Rs. 192.54 crores till 31 st January, 2021. The Committee also notes that against a projected 
Budget Estimate of Rs. 500 crore for the SFRUTI Scheme for FY 2021 -2022, an allocation 
of only Rs. 170 crore has been made. The Committee expresses its concern ove r the low 
utilization pattern and reduction in allocations for an important Scheme of the Ministry, 
which is capable of generating employment in a large scale in the rural areas for the 
artisans, particularly during the Covid Pandemic. The Committee recomm ends that a 
holistic evaluation study of the Scheme may be conducted and based on the said study more 
allocations should be projected by the Ministry at the RE Stage for effective 
implementation of SFURTI Scheme for benefit of the traditional artisans. 
(Para 53) 
 
22. The Committee is constrained to note that out of 371 clusters which have been 
approved, only 82 clusters are operational so far. The Committee recommends that the 
process of setting up of SFURTI clusters should be expedited; targets should be set and 
ensure that the approved clusters are completed and become operational within the 
stipulated timeframe for benefit of artisans.   
(Para 54) 
 
23. The Committee was apprised by the Ministry that besides 219 Districts, 56 
Aspirational Districts have also been covered under SFURTI. The Committee recommends 
that more attention should be paid to target more and more Aspirational Districts across 
the country as this can immensely improve the socio-economic conditions of the inhabitants 
in those districts and improve the human development index. The Ministry may coordinate 
with the state governments and with concerted efforts desired results may be achieved.  
(Para 55) 
 
24. During the Covid Pandemic induced lockdowns, scores of migrant workers were 
forced to return to their native places and had to stay back for months without any 
livelihood/ employment.  SFURTI is one such Scheme which has the potential to generate 
employment in rural areas with less investment for the artisans. The Committee 
recommends that Ministry should endeavour to set up more SFURTI clusters and ensure 
that each and every district of the country has SFURTI clusters on the lines of one -district 
one-product to solve the problem of unemployment in rural areas.   
(Para 56) 
 
25. The Committee observes that one of the most important objectives of the 
implementation of various Schemes under Coir Board is the creation of employment 
especially in rural areas of the country.  For this purpose, Coir Board is providing training 
on various aspects of production and development of new/innovative products. The 
Committee recommends that Ministry should make these training courses popular through 
various social publicity mediums available so that large number of people especially from 
younger generation may get attracted to such training courses which will culminate in 
fruitful employment. 
(Para 61) 

47 
 
26. The Committee notes that export performance of coir and coir products during 
2020-21 is not encouraging, which may be due to Covid Pandemic and consequent 
lockdowns. The Committee recommends that necessary remedial measures may be taken 
by the Coir Board for restoring the export performance as the impact of  Covid is 
improving gradually. Further, the Committee recommends that high targets for exports 
should be set and endeavour should be made to achieve those targets by effective planning 
and execution. Latest technology and techniques should be adopted for m aking coir 
products more competitive to meet the international standards.  
(Para 62) 
 
27. The Committee observes that the Skill Development Programmes organised 
especially in respect of the ‘Physically Handicapped’ Category is not up to the mark. The 
Committee accordingly recommends that more Skill Development Programmes may be 
organized among various categories of people for improving their skills for gainful 
employment in the coir sector. Online training sessions may also be organized as per 
feasibility and practicality. 
(Para 63) 
 
28. The Committee notes that an allocation of Rs. 100 crore was made in BE for Solar 
Charkha Mission for FY 2020 -21 but at the RE Stage it got only Rs. 0.04 crore. Further, 
for FY 2021-22, an allocation of Rs. 5.04 crore has been made at BE Stage. The Committee 
recommends that more budgetary allocations should be made for such a good and eco 
friendly scheme capable of providing employment in rural areas and accordingly, t he 
Ministry should project for more allocations at RE St age for setting up of more Solar 
Charkha Clusters across the country. Besides, the Ministry should provide timely 
interventions so that the Solar Charkha Clusters so set up are operationalized in an 
expeditious manner. 
(Para 65) 
 
29. The Committee desires that the data regarding the CLCS Component may also be 
provided for its perusal thereof. Besides, Technology Upgradation is need of the hour as 
technology is evolving and changing at a fast pace day by day. Moreover technology 
upgradation for MSME Sector i s equally important to keep them competitive in the 
domestic as well as international market. The Committee recommends that some sort of 
international collaboration for technology sharing/transfer should be undertaken for all 
round development of indigenou s MSMEs. Besides, more budgetary allocations should be 
made for adoption of latest and cutting edge technology in view of the changing market 
scenarios.   
(Para 69) 
 
30. The Committee is of the view that for Technology Upgradation, research and 
development are very important for all round development of MSME Sector. The 
Committee therefore, recommends that more funds should be allocated, which is only Rs. 
330.31 crores in the BE for FY 2021-2022 vis-à-vis Rs. 1095.67 crores allocated at RE stage 
in FY 2020-2021, for Technology Upgradation and R&D purposes for strengthening of the 
MSMEs.   

48 
 
(Para 70) 
 
31. During the lockdown periods the availability of raw material was disrup ted which 
affected the operations of MSMEs adversely. Further, the prices of raw material have risen 
exorbitantly in the recent times which have significantly affected the businesses of the 
MSMEs and their profits have significantly decreased. In this give n scenario, NSIC can 
play a significant role by coordinating with the respective Ministries to ensure unhindered 
supply of raw material to MSMEs and also provided support and interventions to the 
MSMEs in the export of their products. The Committee expresses its satisfaction that NSIC 
performed well since II Quarter and facilitated the MSMEs to the tune of Rs. 1234.91 
crores. The Committee is however, of the view that the Ministry should also explore other 
possibilities for raw material supply to MSMEs inst ead of solely depending on NSIC to 
meet the raw material requirements of MSMEs. 
(Para 73) 
 
32. The Committee recommends that a robust procurement system should be evolved 
which could ensure unhindered and timely supply of raw materials to MSMEs at 
reasonable price. The Committee recommends that required steps should be taken to keep 
the prices of raw material reasonable, including giving some sort of subsidy, so that 
MSMEs can run their businesses smoothly.  
(Para 74) 
 
33. The Committee desired that delay in payments by CPSEs and Government 
Departments affects MSMEs adversely as they need cash flow to run their businesses. The 
Committee however, recommends that delayed payments of MSMEs from CPSEs be 
monitored through the SA MBANDH and SAMADHAAN Portals regularly and the 
pending payments of MSMEs may be cleared by CPSEs and other Government agencies at 
the earliest for strengthening the liquidity of MSMEs. 
(Para 78) 
 
34. The Committee notes that TReDS is a new initiative by th e Ministry of MSME for 
resolving the problem of delayed payments to MSMEs by CPSEs/Government Agencies. 
Making penal provision of 1% per month for erring buyers will definitely prove to be a 
deterrent for defaulting buyers. The Committee expects that the p enal provision is 
enforced in letter and spirit. The Committee hopes that TReDS will able to solve the 
problem of delayed payments and improve the liquidity position of the MSMEs. The 
Committee recommends that TReDS should be implemented strictly and monit ored 
regularly and the MSMEs may be exempted from paying charges for on -boarding this 
platform beyond 31st March 2021. 
(Para 79) 
 
35. The Committee observes that NSIC through its Vendor Development Programmes 
sensitize and facilitate MSEs, including SC/ST enterprises, to become qualified vendors to 
public sector enterprises and other Government Departments as per the provision of 25% 
mandatory procurement under Public Procurement Policy. Of this, 4% should be from 
SC/ST MSEs. However, during its visit to Ko lkata, Hyderabad and Mumbai in January, 

49 
 
2020, the Committee found that while the PSUs and Government procurement from MSEs 
has been gradually improving, procurement from SC/ST units is negligible. Therefore, the 
Committee recommends that there should be mo re Vendor Development Programmes 
organized to popularize Public Procurement Policy among MSEs especially SC/ST and 
Women entrepreneurs. 
(Para 83) 
 
36. The Committee notes that the pace of expenditure under the NSCST Hub Scheme is 
not at all encouraging and that the allocation of Rs. 150 crore in the BE 2020-2021 has been 
reduced to Rs. 120 crore at the RE Stage. Further, the allocation for FY 2021 -2022 has also 
been kept at Rs. 120 crore at the BE Stage. The Committee fails to understand the reasons 
for such slow pace of expending in respect of such an important Scheme, which has been 
specially formulated for the marginalized section of the society. The C ommittee 
recommends that the Ministry should take adequate steps to speed up the spending 
process, so that allocated amount gets utilized to the optimum.  
(Para 84) 
 
37. The Committee observes that under National SC/ST Hub, the Actual Expenditure 
has always been less than the BE. The Committee is concerned about the under -utilization 
of allocated funds meant for the marginalized communities of the society. The Committee 
recommends that Ministry should endeavor to improve the situation by ensuring that the 
budget earmarked for SC/ST Hub Scheme is utilized fully for the benefit of the 
communities. Creating awareness among SC/ST entrepreneurs, ground level support and 
handholding of SC/ST entrepreneurs may work well in improving the performance of this 
scheme. Underutilization of funds is a serious cause of concern for the Committee; 
therefore, Ministry is advised to ensure full utilization of funds. 
(Para 85) 
 
38. The Committee recommends that the Ministry should create an All India Database 
of SC/ST entrepreneurs’ locations and vocations and share the same with CPSEs so that 
CPSEs can locate SC/ST units easily for availing their services. Also, the SC/ST Hub 
should run NSQF compliant skill development programmes for SC/ST technicians who 
could take contract jobs and services that CPSEs outsource. 
(Para 86) 
 
39. The trend under Public Procurement Policy has not been encouraging over the 
years. The Committee therefore, recommends that the trend should be reversed and 
adequate steps should be taken by the Ministry to ensure fair participation of SC/ST MSEs 
in Public Procurement Policy.  The Committee also recommends that more special VDPs 
should be organized for SC/ST entrepreneurs for improving their participation in Public 
Procurement Policy. The Ministry  should also adopt handholding approach while 
promoting SC/ST entrepreneurs.   
(Para 87) 
 
40. The Committee observes that many schemes of the Ministry are not working 
satisfactorily in North Eastern Region and has a very negligible presence in these areas.   

50 
 
Even the number of ISEC issued under Khadi and Polyvastra are also not impressive. The 
Committee recommends that serious efforts should be made by the Ministry to benefit the 
people of NER through its various schemes with the help of State Governments 
particularly potential women and SC/ST entrepreneurs be encouraged to participate in the 
growth process. 
(Para 88) 
 
41. The Committee recommends that Testing & Certifications should be made 
convenient and cheaper for MSMEs and they should be provided some sort of subsidy for 
availing such testing facilities. It is also required that a mechanism should be developed so 
that testing can be done at Indian Centres whereas certificates for the same test could be 
issued from various global testing centres, which are acceptable in respective 
countries/regions.  
(Para 90) 
 
42. The Committee notes that Ministry has launched CHAMPIONS Portal for grievance 
redressal of MSME units but many small units are not aware about this portal and its 
functions. The Committee recommends that adequate steps should be taken by the 
Ministry to create awareness about this portal and more budgetary alloc ations be made for 
publicity purposes. The use of the Portal may be made as simple as possible and also the 
portal should have an option for Hindi language as well as the Regional languages for ease 
of understanding. 
(Para 103) 
 
43. As a consequence of COV ID-19 Pandemic and subsequent lockdowns, numerous 
MSMEs became stressed and could not sustain their businesses due to unavailability of 
working capital, raw material and manpower. Accordingly the CGSSD Scheme has been 
designed to infuse capital in the form of subordinate debt to the MSMEs, which have either 
become NPA or are on the verge of becoming NPA,  to help them increase their liquidity. 
The Committee is of the view that the CGSSD Scheme has the capability of providing much 
desired liquidity to the MSMEs who are desperately in need of capital to sustain their 
business. The Committee therefore, recommends that all the procedures and technicalities 
for availing the benefits of the Scheme should be simplified;  irreducible minimum interest 
should be cha rged; repayment tenure of the loan should be kept at the maximum and; a 
friendly and favourable approach should be adopted by the banks to help revive the 
MSMEs. 
    (Para 104)
